parties:
Dipok Kumar Roy
Vs.
Noor Mohammad Yousuf
full_judgment:
Bijan Kumar Das, J: By this rule the opposite party No. 2 was called upon to show cause as to why the impugned judgment and order dated 2.2.02 passed in Other Execution Case No. 1 of 2001 by the Joint District Judge, Court, Chittagong should not be set aside and or pass such other or further order or orders as to this court may seem fit and proper.

2. The predecessor of the present petitioner instituted a suit for specific performance of contract being Other Suit No. 110 of 1979 in the 1st Court of the subordinate Judge, Chittagong and the defendant No. 1 contested the said suit which was dismissed by the trial court. The father of the present petitioner as appellant then preferred Other Appeal No. 411 of 1984 before the learned District Judge, Chittagong and during the pendency of the said appeal the father of the present petitioner died and the present petitioner was substituted in his place. The said Appeal No. 411 of 1984 was ultimately allowed by the Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Chittagong who reversed the decision of the trial Court and decreed the suit for specific performance of contract. Thereafter the present petitioner put the decree in execution being Other Execution Case No. 1 of 2001 in the Court of Joint District Judge, Chittagong. In the said execution case the desired kabala was duly registered as deed No. 6371 dated 16.10.2001. After taking delivery of the registered kabala from the Sub-Registrar's Office the present petitioner being the decree-holder in the suit for specific performance of contract filed an application before the learned Joint District Judge praying for delivery of possession of the suit land. The executing court by the impugned order dated 2.2.02 rejected the prayer for delivery of possession on the ground that the decree does not indicate delivery of possession of the suit land to the decree holder.

3. Being aggrieved thereby the decree holder as petitioner moved this court and obtained the present rule.

4. Mr. Arun Kumar Bhattacharja, the learned Advocate appears with the learned Advocate Mr. Sanjib Kanti Chowdhury for the petitioner. No one entered appearance on behalf of the opposite parties No. 2 though rule was duly served as appears from the office note dated 20.8.02.

5. Mr. Bhattacharja, the learned Advocate for the petitioner argued that order 21 rule. 32(5) of the Code of Civil Procedure provides remedy for a decree holder in a suit for specific performance of contract to get delivery of possession of the suit land. Mr. Bhattacharja submits that there may not to be a clear and specific direction in the decree passed in a suit for specific performance of contract for delivery of possession of the contracted property to the decree holder but the decree may be executed in order to enforce delivery of possession of the property contracted to be sold in view of an implied term of the contract and also an implied term of the decree for specific performance of contract of the said contract.

<u>6. I have considered the submissions of the learned Advocate for the petitioner and perused the impugned order and all other connected papers. There is no dispute that a suit for specific performance of contract was decreed by the appellate court in Other Appeal No. 411 of 1984 on 4.3.99 against the opposite parties, who were defendants in the suit. On the basis of the said decree for specific performance of contract, a registered kabala No. 6371 dated 16.10.2001 was executed in favour of the plaintiff through court and the said registered kabala was delivered to the present petitioner in due course of time. A decree passed in a suit for specific performance of contract indicates that there was a contract between the plaintiff and the defendant No. 1 for transfer of certain property at a certain consideration. The decree further indicates that the defendant No. 1 agreed to transfer the suit land to the deceased father of the present petitioner and according to law when a person agrees to transfer certain property to another he must be deemed to have agreed to do everything to conclude his part of the contract in order to put an end to the agreement of transferring the said property and in order to carry out his primary agreement by a decree made by the court the judgment debtor by necessary implication is due to complete everything for the purpose of concluding the contract entered into between the parties. The decree may not have contained a clear specific term for delivery of possession, yet the executing court in order to give effect to the decree for specific performance of contract should pass necessary orders for delivery of possession of the land under the decree to the decree holder and thereby conclude express or implied term of a contract. The trial court has therefore committed an error of law in refusing delivery of possession of the land in favour of the decree holder on the ground that the decree does not contain any indication for delivery of possession. The executing court has therefore committed an error of law which has resulted in an error in the impugned decision occasioning failure of justice. The view taken above is supported by a decision in the case of Maksud Ali and another Vs. Eskandar Ali reported in 28 DLR(AD)99.</u>

7. In the result this rule is made absolute. The impugned judgment and order dated 2.2.02 passed by the Joint District Judge, Court No. 1, Chittagong in Other Execution Case No. 1 of 2001 is hereby set aside and the executing court is directed to proceed in accordance with law for delivery of possession to the decree holder. In the facts of the case there shall be no order as to costs.

The order of stay of all further proceedings of Other Execution Case No. 1 of 2001 now pending in the 1st Court of the Joint District Judge, Chittagong is hereby vacated.

End.

parties:
Abdul Bashir ------ Petitioner
Vs.
Abdur Rashid and others ------ Opposite parties
full_judgment:
S K Sinha, J: Decree-holder obtained this Rule against the order dated 6.4.2000 of the learned Subordinate Judge, Moulvibazar in Title Execution Case No. 14 of 1985 staying further proceedings of the case till the disposal of Title Suit No. 16 of 2000 pending in the 1st Court of Subordinate Judge, Moulvibazar.

2. Petitioner instituted Title Suit No. 132 of 1972 in the then 1st Court of Munsif, Moulvibazar, for specific performance of contract. The suit was transferred to the Court of 1st Additional Subordinate Judge, Sylhet and was renumbered as Title Suit No. 55 of 1975. The suit was ultimately decreed exparte on 30.11.77 Petitioner thereafter put the decree into execution in Title Execution Case No. 4 of 1979 and obtained a deed executed and registered through court in respect of the suit property on 17.4.83.

3. Opposite parties No. 1-3 thereafter instituted Title Suit No. 182 of 1979 in the then Court of Munsif, Moulvibazar for setting aside the exparte decree on the ground that no summons were served upon them who are bonafide purchasers for value without notice to the previous contract. "The suit was dismissed by judgment and decree dated 4.8.85 on contest. Opposite parties preferred Title Appeal No. 112 of 1985 which was heard by the learned Subordinate Judge, Moulvibazar who by judgment and order dated 26.1.87 allowed the appeal and decreed the suit and set aside the exparte decree dated 4.8.85. Petitioner moved this court in Civil Revision No. 28 of 1987 against the aforesaid judgment and decree. This court upon hearing the parties by judgment and order dated 1.4.97 made the rule absolute and restored the judgment of the trial court dismissing the suit. Opposite parties thereafter preferred a Leave Petition being C.P. No. 379 of 1999 before the Appellate Division against the judgment of the High Court. The Appellate Division by judgment and order dated 12.1.2000 dismissed the said Leave Petition. Subsequently the opposite parties instituted Title Suit No. 16 of 2000 for declaration of title and confirmation of possession in respect of the same subject matter. Petitioner started Execution Case No. 14 of 1985 for delivery of possession of the suit property. The opposite parties No. 1-3 filed an application under Order 21 Rule 29 C.P.C. before the executing court for staying further proceedings of the execution case till disposal of the Title Suit No. 16 of 2000 pending in the Court of Subordinate Judge, Moulvibazar. The learned Subordinate Judge upon hearing the parties by the impugned order dated 6.4.2000 stayed further proceedings of the execution case till the disposal of Title Suit No. 16 of 2000.

4. Being aggrieved by the said order, the petitioner obtained this Rule.

5. Mr. Tabarak Hossain, learned Advocate for the petitioner submits that the learned Subordinate Judge, has committed error of law in staying further proceedings of the execution case for an indefinite period in failing to consider that the opposite parties who are the judgment-debtors after having unsuccessful up to the Appellate Division to set aside the decree, instituted the present suit with a view to frustrate delivery of possession through the process of the court.

6. Mr. Mahbubey Alam, learned Advocate for the opposite parties on the other hand submits that the disposal of the earlier suit instituted by them will not stand in the way in passing a decree in the present suit instituted by them, since said suit was dismissed on technical ground. Mr. Alam further submits that since the executing court has stayed the execution case by order dated 6.4.2000 and the said stay order is still in force, ends of justice demands that the said stay order may be extended for some time and the learned Subordinate Judge be directed to dispose of the suit expeditiously.

7. There is no dispute that petitioner got an exparte decree in Title Suit No. 182 of 1979 in which suit the opposite parties were the parties. It is also not disputed that the opposite parties instituted another suit for setting aside the exparte decree and though the suit was decreed on appeal by the lower appellate court but the said decree has been set aside by this court and the said judgment has been maintained by the Appellate Division. It is also not disputed that the suit land originally belonged to one Probasini Bala Das who allegedly entered into an agreement with the petitioner on 21.7.71 for sale of the suit property and subsequently said Probasini Bala sold the suit property in favour of the opposite parties by registered kabla dated 5.4.72 and delivered possession of the suit property in their favour. Thereafter the petitioner instituted Title Suit No. 132 of 1972 on 25.5.72 i.e. after the execution of the sale deed by Probasini Bala in favour of the opposite parties No. 1-3 in respect of the suit property. It may be pointed out here that in the judgment of this court in Civil Revision No. 2204 of 1991 (Dhaka), this Court observed that the said transfer was made by Probasini Bala in favour of the opposite parties during the pendency of Title Suit No. 132 of 1972 which was though inadvertance.

8. In the back ground of the facts, whether the opposite parties No. 1-3 are entitled to an order of stay of further proceedings of the execution case till the disposal of Title Suit No. 16 of 2000 and whether the learned Sub-ordinate Judge was justified in staying further proceedings of the execution case till the disposal of Title Suit No. 16 of 2000. Opposite parties No. 1-3 instituted the suit on being unsuccessful of their earlier suit, for declaration of title, confirmation of possession and for nullity of the deed No. 1065 dated 17.4.84 obtained by the petitioner through court. In the application it has been stated that the opposite parties had no knowledge about the execution of the agreement dated 21.7.71, they being bonafide purchasers for value without notice to the earlier agreement and since they are in possession of the suit property on the basis of a registered deed over statutory period of limitation, the further proceedings of the execution case are required to be stayed till disposal of the suit. The learned Subordinate Judge stayed the further proceedings of the execution case by the impugned order dated 6.4.2000 on the ground that if the execution case is proceeded with various complications would arise and that ends of justice demands that the execution case should be stayed.

9. Though the petitioner got an exparte decree but the opposite parties failed to get the exparte decree set aside. Mr. Mahbubey Alam however, submits that since the suit was dismissed on technical reasons, present suit is legally maintainable and as a suit is pending the further proceedings of the execution case may be stayed for a limited period. The Appellate Division in C.P. No. 379 of 1999 observed that "in that view of the matter, simple suit for setting aside the decree without filing regular suit for cancellation of registered deed obtained through court is not maintainable." Facts remain that the petitioner got a decree and that the opposite parties failed to get the said exparte decree set aside upto the Appellate Division. In the premises, the holder of the decree should not be deprived of the fruits of the decree unless the person at whose instance the decree is sought to be stayed could have made out a strong case to withhold the holder of the decree from enjoyment of the fruits of the decree. Though the opposite parties are in possession of the suit property on the basis of a registered deed dated 5.4.72 but they have to prove that they are bonafide purchasers for value without notice to the previous agreement. These are matters to be proved by the opposite parties in Title Suit No. 16 of 2000 instituted by them which is pending. Till then, I am of the view that, they have no right to withhold the holder of the decree from enjoying the fruits thereof. If the opposite parties can establish their title, they will get possession through the process of the court.

<u>10. The application for stay was made by the opposite parties under Order 21 Rule 29 C.P.C. A court can stay further proceedings of the execution at the instance of a person against whom the decree was passed if a suit is pending against the holder of the decree in the same court but the court in such cases can stay on such terms as to security or otherwise as it thinks fit. The learned Subordinate Judge without directing opposite parties to furnish any security or otherwise, stayed the execution proceeding. However, the learned Subordinate Judge has directed for expeditious disposal of Title Suit No. 16 of 2000 within 2 months from date of making the order. The impugned order was made on 6.4.2000 and at the time of hearing of this Rule, this court queried to the learned Advocate as to whether the order of the learned Subordinate Judge has been complied with or not. The learned Advocate for the opposite parties could not give any satisfactory reply and I find that the suit is still pending. Therefore, this direction as to expeditious disposal of the suit within 2 months was mere a direction. If the learned Subordinate Judge really wanted to dispose of the suit expeditiously, he could have disposed of the suit by this time but even after expiry of More than 1 year of passing of the said order, he has not disposed of the same. Therefore, I am of the view that the order for expeditious disposal was made by the learned Subordinate Judge to justify the order of stay.</u>

<u>11. It appears from the impugned order that the learned Subordinate Judge stayed further proceedings of the execution case on assigning no ground other than for "ends of justice". Ordinarily when a court has made a mistake the aggrieved party has to get it corrected by appeal or revision or review and invoking inherent power of the Court under section 151 CPC which is intended to secure the ends of justice or to prevent the abuse of process of the court. The ends of justice contemplated under section 151 CPC extend to all the litigating parties before the court and not continued to the right of only one of them. Therefore, section 151 should be applied with great caution and unless the ends of justice require the application. In order to decide whether ends of justice require the application under section 151 CPC to a particular case, the Court has to keep in view not only the interest of the applicant but also that of the other side who may be affected by the order sought to be made under section 151 C.P.C.</u>

12. Considering all those aspects of the matter, I am of the view that the learned Sub-ordinate Judge has committed error of law in staying further proceedings of the execution case till the disposal of the Title Suit No. 16 of 2000. Mr. Mahbubey Alam submits that as the stay order is in force since 6.4.2000, ends of justice require that the said stay order may be extended for a limited period and the trial court may be directed to dispose of the suit. In support of his contention, he has referred a decision in the case of Soleman Miah and others Vs. Ishaque being dead his heirs Jairunnessa and others, 9BLD(AD)73. The facts of this case are distinguishable from the facts of that case in view of the fact that in that case the decree-holder did not challenge the stay order before the High Court Division as well as in the Appellate Division. Considering this aspects, the Appellate Division stayed the proceeding for a limited period. In the facts and circumstances of the case, I am of the view that the learned Subordinate Judge has committed error of law in staying further proceedings of the execution case till the disposal of Title Suit No. 16 of 2000 occasioning failure of justice:

13. In the result, the Rule is made absolute without any order as to costs. The order dated 6.4.2000 of the learned Subordinate Judge, 1st Court, Moulvibazar in Title Execution Case No. 14 of 1985 is set aside. The learned Subordinate Judge, 1st Court, Moulvibazar is directed to dispose of Title Suit No. 16 of 2000 pending before him expeditiously preferably within 3 months from the date of receipt of this judgment without giving any adjournment to the parties taking into consideration that there was an order for expeditious disposal of the suit within 2 months but that order has not been complied with. Mr. Alam submits that the suit cannot be disposed of as the petitioner did not enter appearance in the suit and that the summons of the suit could not be served upon him. The petitioner has constructive notice about the pendency of Title Suit No. 16 of 2000 against him and no summons is required to be served upon him. If the petitioner did not take any step in the suit, the learned Subordinate Judge shall be at liberty to dispose of the suit in accordance with law without awaiting for service return.

End.

Md. Motahar Hossain and others ----- Petitioners
Vs.
Moenuddin Sk. and others ----- Opposite Parties
full_judgment:
Mohammad Fazlul Karim, J: Proforma defendants in a suit for declaration of title filed an application under order I Rule 10 of the Civil Procedure Code praying for transposing them as co-plaintiffs. The said prayer having been rejected by the impugned order this rule was issued. The Rule has been resisted by the heirs of the original defendant No.1 deceased Solaiman stating that the court below was justified in rejecting the application as the same is not in accordance with law and they must claim their share in the suit land separately in the prayer of the plaint and in the absence of any averment as to their claim of share they are not entitled to be added as Co-plaintiffs and the application for transposing is not maintainable.

2. It appears from the impugned order that the learned Assistant Judge without assigning any reasons whatsoever rejected the prayer for transposition simply stating that the prayer for transposing is rejected. It appears from the plaint that the suit has been filed by the plaintiffs for decree in favour of the plaintiffs and these proforma defendants for a declaration that the plaintiffs and those proforma defendants have 16 annas interest in the suit land on the averment of bringing these petitioners with the plaintiffs. This proforma defendant stated that they are residents of Dhaka as the suit was hurriedly filed so they were made proforma defendant but in the suit land as stated in the plaint the claim of the plaintiffs and this proforma defendants are same for which they are to be transposed to the category of the plaintiffs. Thus transposition of the proforma defendant as a co-plaintiffs is necessary for complete adjudication of the question involved in the suit and to avoid any complication in the proceeding.

<u>3. I have perused the copy of the plaint supplied to me and according to averments in the plaint the proforma defendants have identical interest in the suit land as the co owners with the plaintiffs and the prayer in the plaint also has been made for a declaration of title of the proforma defendants along with the plaintiffs statements made in the application for transposition also find support in the statement of the plaint and no further statement need to be made In the plaint or for cause of action and as such ends of justice would be best served if the proforma defendant-petitioners be made co-plaintiffs in the suit by transposition for complete and effectual adjudication of the suit.</u>

4. The learned Assistant Judge in a very slip shot manner and without application of judicial mind failed to exercise his discretion, for which the order rejecting the prayer for transposition is not sustainable in law and the impugned order so far it relates to transposition of the petitioners is liable to be set aside.

5. In view of the above, the Rule is made absolute without any order as to costs. The trial court shall see that the suit is disposed of expeditiously. The order of stay granted by this Court on 11.7.1984 is hereby vacated.

End.

parties:
Assistant Director, Agricultural Extension, Magura ------ Plaintiff-Appellant
Vs.
Sonali Bank, Hat Gopalpur Branch, Jhenaidah and other ------ Defendant-Respondents
full_judgment:
Sheikh Abdul Awal J: This appeal is from the judgment and decree dated 30-11-1995 (decree signed on 3-1-1996) passed by the learned Subordinate Judge, 2nd Court, Magura in Title Suit No. 6 of 1995.

2. The relevant facts briefly are that the appellant herein as plaintiff instituted a suit being Title Suit No. 9 of 1991 in the Court of the then Subordinate judge, 2nd Court, Magura against Sonali Bank, Hat Gopalpur Branch, Jhenaidah and two others for declaration that the judgment and decree dated 28-7-1991 passed by the Artha Rin Adalat in Artha Rin Suit No. 1 of 1990 is not binding upon the plaintiff appellant and the said suit was subsequently renumbered on transfer as Suit No. 6 of 1995. The plaintiff's case, in short, is that the defendant No. 1 obtained a decree for an amount of Taka 4,52,713,88 only from the Artha Rin Adalat, Magura in Artha Rin Suit No. 1 of 1990 impleading the plaintiff appellant as defendant No. 3 although the plaintiff was never assigned as Jute Extension Officer, Magura and that he had no connection with the bank loan in question and, as such, the decree passed by the Artha Rin Adalat, Magura ex-parte against him in Artha Rin Suit No. 1 of 1990 is illegal and the same is not binding upon the plaintiff.

3. Defendant Bank contested the suit by filing written statement denying all the material allegations of the plaint contending, inter alia, that Artha Rin Adalat, Magura committed no illegality in decreeing the Artha Rin Suit against the judgment debtor plaintiff. The suit is barred by law and, as such, the same is liable to be dismissed.

4. At the trial both the parties led evidence to prove their respective cases.

5. The learned Subordinate Judge, 2nd Court, Magura after hearing argument of both the parties and on considering the materials on record by the impugned judgment and decree dated 30-11-1995 dismissed the suit on the ground that the plaintiff filed the suit challenging the judgment and decree dated 28-7-1991 passed by the Artha Rin Adalat, Magura in Artha Rin Suit No. 1 of 1990 which is barred by section 6 of the Artha Rin Ain, 1990.

6. Being aggrieved by the aforesaid impugned judgment and decree dated 30-11-1995, the appellant preferred this first appeal.

7. Mr Bhobesh Chandra Sarker, the learned Deputy Attorney-General appearing on behalf of the plaintiff-appellant on going through impugned judgment and decree together with plaint of the suit finds it difficult to assail the impugned judgment. He, however, submits that under the facts and circumstances of the case, the plaintiff-appellant ought to have filed appeal against the impugned judgment and decree dated 30-11-1995 and at this stage the plaintiff-appellant may be given an opportunity to file appropriate case otherwise, the plaintiff-appellant shall suffer irreparable loss.

8. Heard the learned Deputy Attorney-General and perused the record.

9. To cut short the matter at the very outset, we like to quote hereunder the prayer portion of the plaint of the instant Title Suit No. 9 of 1991 which was subsequently re-numbered on transfer as Suit No. 6 of 1995, which reads as follows:-

“…...……বাদীপক্ষ প্রার্থনা করেন যে, (ক) আরজীর বর্ণিত মতে ও কারনে মোকাম মাগুরার অর্থ ঋণ আদালতের ১/৯০ অর্থ ঋণ মামলার ইং ২৮-৭-৯১ তাং এর রায় ও ইং ৪-৮-৯১ তারিখের ডিক্রি বাদী পক্ষের প্রতি binding  বা বাধ্যকর নহে মর্মে বিবাদীপক্ষের বিরুদ্ধে বাদী পক্ষের অনুকুলে ঘোষনার ডিক্রি দিতে-

(খ) যাবতীয় আদালত ব্যায়ের ডিক্রি দিতে-

(গ) Law and Equity মতে বাদীপক্ষ আর যে কেন্যে প্রকার প্রতিকার পাইতে পারেন তাহারও আদেশ দিতে মর্জি হয় ৷”

10. From the above, it transpires that the plaintiff filed the suit challenging the judgment and decree dated 28-7-1991 (decree signed on 4-8-1991) passed by the Artha Rin Adalat, Magura in Artha Rin Case No. 1 of 1990.

11. On scrutiny of the impugned judgment, it appears that the trial Court dismissed the suit on the finding that the suit is barred by section 6 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 1990 inasmuch as the plaintiff filed the suit challenging the judgment and decree dated 28-7-1991 passed by the Artha Rin Adalat, Magura in Artha Rin Suit No. 1 of 1990.

12. Now, let us look at the relevant provisions of both the old and new Artha Rin Adalat Ain for having a better view of the dispute in question.

13. Section 6 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 1990 reads as follows:

“৬ ৷ অর্থ ঋণ আদালতের সিদ্ধান্ত চুড়ান্ত ৷-(১) ধারা ৭ এর বিধান সাপেক্ষে, অর্থ ঋণ আদালতের কার্য্যধারা, আদেশ, রায় ও ডিক্রী সম্পর্কে কোন আদালত বা অন্য কোন কর্তৃপক্ষের নিকট প্রশ্ন উত্থাপন করা যাইবে না ৷

(২) উপ-ধারা (১ ) এ যাহা কিছুই থাকুক না কেন, কোন অর্থ ঋণ আদালত কর্তৃক বিবাদীর বিরুদ্ধে প্রদত্ত কোন একতরফা ডিক্রী রদ করার জন্য বিবাদী Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 (Act V of 1903) এর Order IX এর rule 13 এর বিধান মোতাবেক আদালতে দরথাস্ত করিতে চাহিলে তাহাকে তাহার বিরুদ্ধে ডিক্রীকৃত অর্থের অন্ততঃ অর্ধেক অর্থ বা উহার সমপরিমান অর্থের ব্যাংক জামানত দরখান্তের সহিত আদালতে জমা করিতে হইবে, এবং উক্তরুপ জমা করা না হইলে তাহার দরখাস্ত গ্রহন যোগ্য হইবে না ।”

14. Similar provision has also been provided in sections 19 and 20 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 which read as follows:

১৯ ৷ একতরফা ডিক্রী সম্পতি বিধান ৷-(১) মামলার শুনানীর জন্য ধার্য কোন তারিখে বিবাদী আদালতে অনুপস্থিত থাকিলে, কিংবা মামলা শুনানীর জন্য গৃহীত হইবার পর ডাকিয়া বিবাদীকে উপস্থিত পাওয়া না গেলে, আদালত মামলা একতবফা সূত্রে নিঃষ্পত্তি করিবে।

(২) কোন মামলা একতরফা সূত্রে ডিক্রী হইলে, বিবাদী উক্ত একতরফা ডিক্রীর তারিখের অথবা উক্ত একতরফা ডিক্রী সম্পর্কে অবগত হইবার ৩০(ত্রিশ) দিবসের মধ্যে, উপ-ধারা (৩) এর বিধান সাপেক্ষে, উক্ত একতরফা ডিক্রী রদের জন্য দরখাস্ত করিতে পারিবেন ৷

(৩) উপ-ধারা (২) এর বিধান অনুযায়ী দরখাস্ত দাখিলের ক্ষেত্রে বিবাদীকে উক্ত দরখাস্ত দাখিলের তারিখের পরবর্তী ১৫(পনের) দিবসের মধ্যে ডিক্রীকৃত অর্থের ১০% এর সমপরিমান টাকা বাদীর দাবীর সেই পরিমাণের জন্য স্বীকৃতিস্বরূপ নগদ সংশ্লিষ্ট আর্থিক প্রতিষ্ঠানে, অথবা জামানত স্বরুপ ব্যাংক ড্রাফট পে-অর্ডার বা অন্য কোন প্রকার নগদায়নযোগ্য বিনিমেয় দলিল (Negotiable Instrument) আকারে জামানত হিসাবে আদালতে জমাদান করিতে হইবে ৷

15. Section 20 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 reads as follows:

২০ ৷ অর্থ ঋণ আদালতের আদেশের চূড়ান্ত ৷-এই আইনের বিধান ব্যতিরেকে, কোন আদালত বা কর্তৃপক্ষের নিকট অর্থ ঋণ আদালতে বিচারাধীন কোন কার্যধারা বা উহার কোন আদেশ, রায় বা ডিক্রীর বিষয়ে কোন প্রশ্ন উত্থাপন করা যাইবে না এবং এই আইনের বিধানকে উপেক্ষা করিয়া কোন আদালত বা কর্তৃপক্ষের নিকট আবেদন করিয়া কোন প্রতিকার দাবী বা প্রার্থনা করা হইলে, ঐরুপ আবেদন কোন আদালত বা কর্তৃপক্ষ গ্ৰাহ্য করিবে না ।

<u>16. From a plain reading of the above quoted provisions of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, it appears that except the provisions of this Act, no question shall be raised before any court or authority about any pending proceeding in the Artha Rin Adalat, or its order, judgment or decree, and if any relief is claimed or prayed before any Court or authority ignoring the provisions of this Act, no Court or authority shall accept any such prayer since the judgment or decree of the Artha Rin Adalat is final and the same cannot be questioned in any other Court under any separate proceeding. If any party is aggrieved by the judgment and decree of the Artha Rin Adalat he may prefer appeal against the same as per specific provisions of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain and in case of ex-parte decree, the judgment debtor may prefer an application under section 19 the of Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 for setting-aside the ex-parte decree upon deposit of certain amount as per the said provisions of law. Therefore, we are led to hold that the suit filed by the plaintiff-appellant challenging the judgment and decree passed by the Artha Rin Adalat was expressly barred by specific provisions of both old and new Artha Rin Adalat Ain. Accordingly, we find no reason to differ with the view taken by the trial Court below that the suit filed by the plaintiff challenging the judgment and decree dated 28-7-1991 passed by the Artha Rin Adalat, Magura in Artha Rin Suit No. 1 of 1990 was expressly barred by section 6 of the Artha Rin Ain Adalat, 1990.</u>

17. In view of our discussions made in the forgoing paragraphs it is by now clear that the instant appeal must fail.

18. In the result, the appeal is dismissed without any order as to costs. The impugned judgment and decree dated 30-11-1995 (decree signed on 3-1-1996) passed by the learned Subordinate Judge, 2nd Court, Magura in Title Suit No. 6 of 1995 is affirmed.

19. However, in the facts and circumstances of the case the plaintiff appellant may avail the remedy of appeal against the judgment and decree dated 28-7-1991 passed by the Artha Rin Adalat, Magura in Artha Rin Suit No. 1 of 1990, if he so advised and if it is open to him.

Let a copy of this judgment along with the lower Court's record be sent down at once.

End.

full_judgment:
Md. Joynul Abedin, J: This Rule at the instance of the pre-emptor petitioners calls in question the orders dated 9.6.85 and 30.11.8 passed in Miscellaneous Case No 521 of 1981 refusing to interfere with the order restoring the afore said Misc. case which was dismissed for default on 25.2.85.

2. Fact relevant for the purpose of disposal of the present rule is stated as follows:-

Pre-emptor-petitioners filed pre-emption Misc. Case No. 58 of 1981 under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act in the Court of Munsif, Gazipur seeking pre-emption of the case land. The aforesaid pre-emption Misc. case was decreed exported by order date 28.11.81. The pre-emptee-opposite parties No. 1 to 3, therefore, file an application under Order 9, Rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure being Misc. Case No. 521 of 1981 for setting aside the exported decree. But the said Misc. case was dismissed for default by order dated 25.2.85.

3. The pre-emptee opposite parties thereafter filed an application for review under Order 47, Rule 1 read with section 114 and 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure in terms of Order 47 Rule 2 for restoration of the said misc. case on review of the dismissal order dated 25.2.85. But the trial Court by order dated 2 1.5.85 rejected the same as not maintainable. Subsequently, pre-emptee-Opposite parties No. 1-3 filed an application under section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure on 9.6.85 for restoration of the Misc. case on reconsideration of the said order dated 21.5.85. Trial Court, thereupon, by order dated 9.6.85 restored the aforesaid Misc. Case No. 521 of 1981 by allowing the said application under section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure.

4. The pre-emptor petitioner being aggrieved by the said order dated 9.6.85 filed an application under Section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure for correcting the afore-said order dated 9.6.85 but the same was rejected by order dated 30.11.85 on the ground that the same court could not interfere with its earlier order. The pre-emptor petitioners having been aggrieved filed the instant revision and obtained the present Rule.

5. Learned Advocate Mr. Kazi Shahadat Hossain, appearing on behalf of the pre-emptor petitioners submits that the pre-emptee-opposite parties i to 3 wrongly filed the application for review of the order dated 25.2.85 dismissing the said Misc. Case for default inasmuch such dismissal order was liable to be challenged by filing appeal only under Order 43 Rule 1(d). Hence, the court below was justified in rejecting the application for review by order dated 21.5.85 as not maintainable. It is urged by Mr. Hossain that since the order dated 21.5.85 rejecting the application for review was rightly made, the pre-emptee opposite parties could challenge the said order dated 21.5.85 by filing a revision and not by filing an application under Section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure for reconsideration of the said order dated 21.5.85. The court below in the circumstances, having restored the said Misc. case by allowing the aforesaid application under section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure has committed an error of law occasioning failure of justice.

6. Learned Advocate Kazi Shahadat Hossain cited a decision in the case of Pujari Chatur Bhuj Vs. Saiyda Jobeda Begum reported in 22 D.L.R. (1970) 383 in support of his contention that the order dated 21.5.85 being an order of rejection the application for review under Order 47, rule 1 or an application under section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure was not competent except a civil revisional application under section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure. It is contended by the learned Advocate that Section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure cannot be resorted to when there is a specific forum provided by law inasmuch as the same cannot be resorted to when there is a specific forum provided by law inasmuch as the same cannot be treated as an alternative mode for seeking redress. Learned Advocate for the pre-emptor-petitioners also relied on a decision reported in the case of Md. Hossain Mollah & others Vs. Asstt. Deputy Custodian reported in 37 D.L.R. (1985) 287 to strengthen his point already advanced that provision under section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure is only available to rectify any wrong when there is no remedy under the law and that the same cannot be pressed into service to further injustice or to condone gross negligence.

7. In the case of Pujari Chatur Bhuj Das Vs. Saiyeda Jobeda Begum reported in 22 D.L.R. (1970) 383, the plaintiff filed Title Suit No. 10 of 1960 and the same was decreed ex-parte as the defendants failed to take any step. Hence, the defendant filed an application under section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure for setting aside the exported decree contending that the said Title Suit was to be taken and heard analogously with Title Suit No. 106 of 1959 as per order of the District Judge. But it was not done. Hence the defendant was not aware of the date of hearing. The trial Court re-fused to entertain such application on the ground that the defendants ought to have taken appropriate steps for setting aside the expert decree either by instituting a Misc. case under Order 9 rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure or by filing an appeal. A Single Bench of the then High Court at Dhaka Presided over by Mr. Justice Maksumul-Hakim in his revisional jurisdiction affirmed the above decision of the trial Court as under:-

"In my opinion, the stand taken by the learned Sub-ordinate Judge in this case is clearly legal and valid. A proceeding under section 151 Civil Procedure Code cannot be taken when there are other remedies available for securing the redress. The inherent power conferred on the Court under Section 151 Civil Procedure Code should only be resorted to in a case where there is no other provision or procedure for pro-viding redress or rectifying a clear injustice. It is never as alternative mode for securing relief."

8. In the case of Md. M. Hossain Mollah & ors Vs. Asstt. Dy. Custodian reported in 37 D.L.R. (1985)287 a similar view was taken by a single bench of this Division which is evident from the passage quoted below:-

"From the decisions quoted above it is clear that when a party had got a right of appeal against the order he should go for an appeal, he cannot maintain an application under section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure for reversal of the expert order. In the instant case, the learned Munsif exercise his jurisdiction with material irregularity in allowing the said application under section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure. It was just and proper for restoration of a case under Order 9 r. 13 of the Code of Civil procedure but it is not just and proper to entertain the application for restoration under Order 9, rule 4 of the Code of Civil Procedure and under section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure. Order 7 rule 4 of the Code of Civil Procedure provides for the plaintiff to bring a fresh suit which is dismissed either for non-service of summons in consequence of plaintiffs failure to pay cost or for non-appearance of both the plaintiff and defendants. In this connection, application under section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure is also not maintainable, because inherent power of the court exists only where there is no express provision of law applicable to the case. The provisions of this section cannot be invoked to defeat the provisions of the Code nor can be invoked to further injustice or to condone gross negligence. The court cannot interfere under section 151 of the Code with appealable order-.

9. Mr. Md. Ashfaqul Islam, learned Advocate for the pre-emptee opposite parties in reply submits that the order dated 25.2.85 dismissing the Misc. case was an appealable order in terms of Order 43, rule 1(d). But without filing any appeal an application for review was made for setting aside the said dismissal order in terms of Order 47, rule 1(2) of the Code of Civil Procedure and as such the prayer for review was competent. Hence, the court below was not justified in rejecting the application for review as not maintainable vide order dated 21.5.85. Accordingly, it as submitted, an application under section151 of the Code of Civil Procedure was filed by the pre-emptee opposite parties for restoration of the said misc. case on reconsideration of the said order dated 21.5.85. Learned Advocate for the pre-emptee opposite parties submits without disputing the Principle of law that ordinarily provision under section 151 of the Code cannot be restored to where there is specific forum provided for in law, but in a case where the court has passed a mistaken order affecting rights of a party in the proceeding redress can be had by resorting to section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure without availing of other remedies or forum namely revision or appeal which is inconvenient or otherwise time consuming or even expensive. The learned Advocate for the pre-emptee- opposite parties further submits that in a case where a wrong or mistaken order of the court has caused prejudice to the party in the preceding the same court can rectify the situation by acting ex debits justified. In support of his aforesaid submissions the learned Advocate placed reliance on two decisions in the case of Atash Ali and others Vs. Rebati Mohan Sarker and 3 others reported in 43 D.L.R. (1991)539 arid the case of Mohan Bashi Saha Vs. United Bank of India Ltd. & others reported in 15 D.L.R. (1963)383.

10. In the aforesaid case of Atash Ali and others Vs. Rebati Mohan Sarker and 3 others a single Bench of this Division held as under:-

"Where the Court itself passed a wrong order the court is competent to rectify the said order upon an application filed u/s. 151 C.P.C. by either party to the proceeding or suo-motu by invoking its inherent power under section 151 of the Code and exercise of such power is no error of law, rather by such exercise of power the Court does real and substantial justice for the administration of which the Court exists. Such exercise of power is in consonance with the principle acts curiae neminem Gravabit an act of court shall prejudice none. In that view of the matter 1 do not find any error of law in the decision occasioning failure of justice in making the impugned order."

11. In the aforesaid case of Mohan Bashi Saha Vs. United Bank of India Ltd. and others Mr. Justice Idris, while delivering a judgment of a Division Bench sitting with Mr. Justice Hasan held as under:-

"The jurisdiction of the Court to act ex debit justified cannot be ousted simply because another inconvenient remedy is also available".

12. In the present case the pre-emptee opposite parties instituted Misc. Case No. 521 of 1981 under Order 9, Rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure for setting aside the expert decree passed in the pre-emption case filed by the pre-emptor petitioner. The said Misc. case was dismissed for default by the trial Court on 25.2.85 for non-appearance of the pre-emptee opposite parties. The said order dated 25.2.85 was an appealable order in terms of Order 43, rule 1(d) of the Code of Civil Procedure. But in terms of the Order 47, rule 1(2) of the Code of Civil Procedure the pre-emptee-opposite parties were competent to file an application for review under order as he did not file any appeal, which was precisely done in this case by the pre-emptee-opposite parties.

13. Order 47, Rule 1(2) of the Code of Civil Procedure provides as under:

"A party who is not appealing from a decree or order may apply for a review of judgment notwithstanding the pendency of an appeal by some other party except where the ground of such appeal is common to the applicant and the appellant or when, being respondent, he can present to the appellate Court the case on which he applies for the review".

14. Inspire of the fact that review application in the present case was competent the trial court by order dated 21.5.85 rejected such application filed by the pre-emptee opposite parties as not maintainable, which in fact affected their right and interest. It is not, however, denying the fact that the pre-emptee-opposite parties could file a civil revisional application challenging the aforesaid order of dismissal dated 21.5.85 for unduly rejecting the application for review. But in-stead of doing that they filed an application under section 151 of the Code at Civil Procedure which was less expensive and convenient and speeder in the facts and circumstances of the case. 1. respectfully agree with the law laid down in the case of Atash Ali & others Vs. Rebati Mohan Sarker and 3 others reported in 43 D.L.R (19911539 and Mohan Bashi Saha Vs. United Bank of India Ltd. & others reported in 15 D.L.R. (1963)383, that when a mistaken order has caused injustice to a party such order can be set aside by invoking inherent jurisdiction of the Court or in acting ex debito justified for remedying such injustice.

15. Our Appellate Division also agreed with the aforesaid position in the case of Panjab Ali Vs. Mohd. Mokarram Hossain reported in 29 D.L.R. (SC)(1977) 185. The relevant paragraph of the judgment thereof is reproduced below:-

"The Court should not presume the existence of inherent power to do that for which specific provision has been made by a statute and should not invest itself with such jurisdiction for the purpose of getting round the ex-press provisions of the law. Unintentional or inadvertent mistake of a Court causing injustice to a party, however stands on a different footing and in the case of such a mistake the exercise of inherent power of a Court is not subject to those limitations on its exercise which have been set down by the judicial authorities noticed above."

<u>16. Since the court below through inadvertence or mistake disallowed the review application for restoration of Misc. case No. 521 of 1981 although such application was competent in law the court below subsequently having restored the same by allowing the application under section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure committed no error of law occasioning failure of justice.</u>

17. In the result, the Rule is discharged without any order as to cost.

18. The trial Court is directed to proceed with Miscellaneous Case No. 521 of 1981 in accordance with law.

19. The order of stay earlier passed by this Court staying all further proceedings of Misc. Case No. 521 of 1981 at the time of issuance of the rule is hereby vacated.

Let the lower court records be sent down expeditiously.

End.

full_judgment:
Md Khasruzzaman J: The above noted first appeal, at the instance of the plaintiff Mirpur section No. 6 Bohumukhi Samabai Samity Ltd, was preferred against the judgment and decree dated 6-6-2012 (decree signed on 14-6-2012) passed by the Joint District Judge, Additional Court, Dhaka in Title Suit 14 of 2012 analogously heard and disposed of with Title Suit No. 13 of 2012 (Md Nazrul Islam vs Mirpur Section No. 6 Bohumukhi Samabai Samity Ltd.) decreeing the suit (Title Suit No. 14 of 2012) by awarding Taka 85,45,000 in favour of the plaintiff-samity.

2. The plaintiff-samity instituted Title Suit No. 46 of 2005 on 9-2-2005 for specific performance of contract impleading the vendor Md Nazrul Islam as principal defendant. Subsequently, the suit was renumbered as Title Suit No. 14 of 2012 on transfer to the Additional Court of Joint District Judge, Dhaka.

3. Prior to filing of the suit, the vendor Md Nazrul Islam had instituted Title Suit No. 383 of 2004 impleading the samity as defendant for a declaration that the contract for sale in question was void and not binding upon him. The suit was also renumbered as Title Suit No. 13 of 2012 on transfer to the same Court.

4. The case of the plaintiff-samity is same as that of defendant No. 1 in Title Suit No. 13 of 2012 and the case of the plaintiff-vendor in Title Suit No. 13 of 2012 is same as that of defendant No. 1 in Title Suit No. 14 of 2012. Both the suits were heard analogously and were disposed of by a single judgment dated 6-6-2012.

5. The case of the plaintiff-samity, in short, is that the suit land belonged to the Government in the Settlement and Housing Department under the Ministry of Works, which leased out the same to one Gazanfar Ali for 99 years and handed over the possession thereof. The said Gazanfar Ali made construction on the suit land according to a plan approved by RAJUK. The vendor Md. Nazrul Islam purchased the suit property from the said Gazanfar Ali by a registered sale deed being No. 4278 dated 15-10-1992, and constructed a multi-storied building thereon as per a revised plan duly approved by RAJUK. The General Secretary of the plaintiff-samity Mr Md Abdul Manna, and a member Md. Sobhan purchased the possession of shop Nos. 1 and 2 respectively situated on the ground floor. The vendor, Md Nazrul Islam, executed an instrument of transfer of possession on 22-2-1993 to that effect. Subsequently, he obtained loan of Taka 25,00,000 lakh from Janata Bank, Mirpur Branch (defendant No. 4 in Title Suit No. 14 of 2012) on 19-11-1997 and mortgaged the suit property to the bank as security suppressing the fact of selling possession of two shops. In order to complete the construction of the six-storied building, he also took loan from the plaintiff-samity, and sold possession of the first and second floors to seventy shareholders of its Commercial Project No. 1 for consideration of Taka 7,00,000 (seven lakh) on 3-3-1998 and Taka 7,00,000 (seven lakh) on 23-5-1998 respectively. The .vendor Md Nazrul Islam entered into an agreement for sale of the third floor to one Md Manir-ul-Islam and Md Abdul Quaiyum on 18-6-1998 and received Taka 7,50,000 lakh (seven lakh fifty thousand) from them, who subsequently transferred the possession of the 3rd (third) floor to the samity on receiving Taka 7,50,000 lakh (seven lakh fifty thousand). Then he took Taka 5,50,000 lakh (five lakh fifty thousand) on 4-1-1999 from one Md Mobin Khan, a member of the samity for transfer of possession of the fourth floor and took Taka 4,25,000 (four lakh twenty-five thousand) from the samity for transfer of the possession of the fifth floor, which was still under construction. In this way the vendor received Taka 36,01,000 in total from the samity and some of its members for transfer of possession of all the floors of the building.

6. Thereafter, he entered into an agreement for sale of the suit property to the samity at a consideration of, Taka- 85,50,000 (eighty-five lakh fifty thousand) and handed over its possession to the samity. It was stipulated that the vendor, after obtaining sale permission from Housing and Settlement. Directorate, would execute and register, a proper sale deed, but took no, measures to that effect. He also shifted his liability to Janata Bank upon the samity, and accordingly a tri-partite negotiation between the bank, vendor and samity was held on 28-2-1999 at Janata Bank, Mirpur-10 Branch and an adjustment of the liability regarding the vendor's bank loan was undertaken by the samity in writing. The samity accordingly paid the entire loan of the vendor amounting to Taka 24,52,556 (twenty-four lakh fifty-two thousand five hundred fifty-six) in total to the bank. The vendor himself also received Taka 24,30,000 (twenty-four lakh thirty thousand) in cash and Taka 25,00,000 (twenty-five lakh) by way of refund of bank loan and additional amounts of Taka 36,01,000 from time to time from the samity and acknowledged receipts thereof. Thereafter, he received some more amount from the samity. The total amounts taken by him thus Comes to Taka 85,45,000 (eighty-five lakh forty-five thousand). As he refused to execute the sale deed, the samity was constrained to tile: Title Suit No. 14 of 2012.

7. The vendor Md Nazrul Islam contested the suit by filing a written statement contending, inter alia, that the suit land belonged to the Housing and Settlement Directorate under the Ministry of Housing and Public Works, who leased it out to one Gazanfar Ali, from whom he had purchased the suit property by a registered sale deed dated 15-10-1992 and constructed a multi-storied building thereon as per revised construction plan duly approved by RAJUK.

8. Thereafter he fell in need of money and the samity offered him to pay off the debt, which he owed to Janata Bank, keeping that in consideration the vendor signed and executed two agreements for sale dated 17-2-1999 and 14-3-2000. Although the said two deeds contained the recital of receiving Taka 85,45,000 in total as main part of the consideration, in fact he had received Taka 15,00,000 (fifteen lakh). The samity though undertook to repay the loan to the bank, did not do so and now the bank is pressurizing him for repayment of the loan.

9. The samity has been misappropriating lakhs of money by continuing its forceful and illegal possession over the property, which compelled him to institute Title Suit No. 13 of 2012 for a declaration that the agreement for sale is not binding on him. The samity instituted the present Title Suit No. 14 of 2012 for specific performance of contract just to frustrate his suit. Thus he prayed for dismissal of Title Suit No. 14 of 2012.

10. The proforma defendant Nos. 2 and 3 (in Title Suit No. 14 of 2012), the Chairman, National Housing Authority and its Director, Land and Estate Management in their joint written statement, amongst others, stated that the suit land was allotted to one Gazanfar Ali by a letter of allotment dated 18-7-1981 and the possession thereof was handed over to him on 19-10-1981. Thereafter, a lease deed being No. 1361 dated 13-3-1989 was executed and registered in his favour after payment of the total consideration money got a plan approved by RAJUK for construction of a seven-storied building thereon. He, however, sold out the suit land by a registered sale deed being No. 4278 dated 15-10-1992 to Md Nazrul Islam (the principal defendant in Title Suit No. 14 of 2012). He got the record mutated in his name by filing an application on 12-7-1992 and obtained a non-encumbrance certificate on 24-6-1997. They had no knowledge of the agreement for sale as no application seeking sale permission was filed to them. If anyone wants to sell a plot/house/flat under their control, he is to pay a particular amount of fees on deposition of which, the authority gives him the sale permission. There is no provision to sell a plot/house/flat without any sale permission.

11. Proforma defendant No 4 Janata Bank in its written statement stated, inter alia, that the bank sanctioned Taka 25,00,000 (twenty-five lakh) on 16-11-1997 in favour of Md. Nazrul Islam. He wrote a letter to the bank on 28-2-1999 that Mirpur section No. 6 Bohumukhi Samabaya Samity Ltd. would repay the loan. The entire loan inclusive of interest was paid by the President, Secretary and Joint Secretary of the samity.

12. To prove their respective claims Md Abdul Mannan, General Secretary of the plaintiff-samity in Title Suit No. 14 of 2012 and Md Nazrul Islam, plaintiff in Title Suit No. 13 of 2012 were examined as witnesses.

13. Md Abdul Mannan PW 1 in his deposition supported the plaint case described in Title Suit No. 14 of 2012 and produced some documents which were marked as exhibit Nos. 1, 2- 2(Gha), 3, 4-4 (Ka), 5, 6, 7-7 (Gha), 8-8(Ga), 9-9 (Ha), 10, 11,12.

14. On the other hand Md. Nazrul Islam deposed in Title Suit No.14 of 2012 as DW 1. In his evidence he stated that he had executed the agreements for sale after receiving the earnest money and handed over possession of the scheduled property in favour of the plaintiff-samity and also executed a nadabipatro in support of the proposed sale. His wife, son and daughter were the witnesses to the said nadabipatro. On perusal of the record we have also found that the vendor entered into two agreements with the plaintiff-samity for sale of the suit property and also executed and signed a na-dabinama in favour of the samity. The vendor admitted the execution of the agreement but disputed receipt of certain amount of money and entries on the agreement. So the submission of the learned Advocate for the respondent that the vendor was not in a position either to check the correctness of the entries or to go through the contents of the document and since he had no equal bargaining power, his consent was not free, and it rather was obtained by some other manner indicating fraud, is not acceptable.

<u>36. It is true that section 108 of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882 does not allow a lessee to transfer his interest unless he is authorized to do so by the lessor. In the present case no sale permission is given by the Housing Authority and the transfer without written permission is also restricted expressly by the lease deed. The sale permission was a condition precedent to transfer the land and admittedly no permission has been given. But mere signing of the contract was not sale, it was an agreement for sale and the permission is yet to be accorded. According to the cases of Motilal vs Nanhelal, 35 CWN 93, and Gokul vs Haji, 42 CWN 97 cited by the plaintiff-appellant, the civil Court is competent to pass a decree for specific performance and to direct the vendor to execute and register the sale deed after obtaining sale permission from the authority concerned and redemption of the mortgage from the bank within a specified time failing which the plaintiff will be entitled to get the sale deed executed and registered through Court, and in that event the proforma defendants will be bound to accord necessary permission for sale and to redeem the mortgage property in compliance with the decree. We are in agreement with the above cited decisions.</u>

<u>37. Explanation to section 12 of the Specific Relief Act provides that the breach of contract to transfer immovable property cannot adequately be compensated by money. This view finds support from the cases of Sudbrook Trading Estate vs Eggleton, [1983] 1 AC 44 and Bazlur Rahman vs BS Corporation, 34 DLR (AD) 42.</u>

38. It appears from the transaction of the parties that the plaintiff appellant paid the consideration money phase by phase and took delivery of possession of the property. The defendant-respondent vendor did not receive the consideration money at a time. The defendant vendor constructed the building by taking loans and after completing construction he transferred the same. He could not enjoy the property. Due to payment of consideration money phase by phase he has suffered financial loss and a considerable portion of the consideration money was repaid against the loan. In such circumstance we are of the view that an amount as solatium should be given to the defendant-respondent.

39. We find substance in the submissions of the learned Advocate for the appellant and as such the plaintiff is entitled to get a decree as prayed for.

40. In the result, the First Appeal No. 267 of 2012 is allowed and the Title Suit No.14 of 2012 is decreed. The Cross Objection No. 2 of 2013 is dismissed without any order as to costs.

41. The defendant-respondent vendor Md Nazrul Islam is directed to execute and register a sale deed in respect of the scheduled property in favour of the plaintiff-samity on receipt of Taka 20,00,000 (twenty lakh) as solatium after obtaining sale permission from the National Housing Authority and redemption of the mortgaged property from the bank within 3 (three) months from the date of receipt of the judgment, failing which the plaintiff-samity is entitled to get the sale deed registered through Court.

42. Respondent Nos. 2 and 3 National Housing Authority and Respondent No. 4, Janata Bank, Mirpur section 10 Branch respectively are directed to accord the sale permission and redeem the mortgaged property in favour of the vendor Md Nazrul Islam.

Send down the lower court's records.

End.

parties:
Mokseda Bewa and another ----- Petitioner
Vs.
Amela Khatun and others ----- Opposite Parties
full_judgment:
M. M. Ruhul Amin, J: This rule was issued calling upon the opposite party Nos. 1 and 2 to show cause as to why the impugned judgment and order no. 16 dated 19.5.96 passed in Misc. Case No. 45 of 1994 by the learned District Judge, Sirajganj rejecting the application of the petitioners for withdrawing S.C.C. Suit No. 4 of 1985 from the Court of Assistant Judge, Sirajganj Sadar, Sirajganj filed by the opposite party no. 2 and hearing the said case analogously with the Other Class Suit No. 54 of 1993 pending the Senior Assistant Judge, Sirajganj Sadar, Sirajganj filed by the petitioner No. 1 or such other or further order or orders passed as to this court may seem fit and proper.

2. Facts relevant for the purpose of disposal of the rule are as follows:-

The schedule land originally belonged to one Kaliganga Devi who died leaving two sons, Suresh Chandra Bhattacharya and Parash Chandra Bhattacharya opposite party Nos. 3 and 4 respectively. While they were in peaceful possessions of the said property the then landlords Hem Chandra Chowdhury and others instituted Rent Suit No. 126 of 1951 in the Court Munsif 2nd Court Sirajganj for arrear rents and got an exparte decree. The property was then sold in auction in Rent Execution Case No. 1835/44 and the petitioner no. 1 as 3rd party Mokseda Khatun auction purchased the land on 22.11.44. The sale was duly confirmed on 23.12.44 and the auction purchaser got khas possession of the land through her husband amicably with the judgment debtors and inducted a monthly tenant Borjo Ballav Kundu in the property. Thereafter Patna District Administration requisitioned the entire suit property vide Requisition case no. 23 of 1960 but the Requisition case was wrongly started in the names of the Judgment debtors Suresh and Paresh Chandra Battachariya of the Rent suit. The husband of the opposite party no. 1 manufactured some ante-date pattani likhan and Dakhilas regarding the suit land in favour of his wife and ultimately filed O.C. suit no. 103 of 1975 claiming the land on the basis of pattani likhan and obtained an exparte decree. The opposite party no. 1 then created a deed of sale dated 8.9.77 in favour of the daughter opposite party no. 2 without receiving any consideration money. The opposite Party no. 2 thereafter instituted O.C. Suit No. 645 of 1978 in the 2nd Court of Munsif Sirajganj claiming that she had been in peaceful possession of the entire suit property since her alleged purchase from her mother. The petitioner no. 2 at the relevant time was an allottee with respect to the suit property from the Government and as such he filed a petition under Order 1 Rule 10 of the Code of Civil Procedure for adding as defendant in the suit. The trial court allowed the petition and impleads him as defendant. But due to objection raised by the otherside his name was struck off from the defendant's list of the said O.C. Suit No. 645 of 1978 and the suit was decreed on 22.12.80

3. While the petitioner no. 2 was living in the suit property as allottee of the Government the petitioner no. 1 exchanged suit property with agricultural property of the petitioner no. 2 on 28.2.83. Thereafter opposite party no. 2 filed S.C.C. suit No. 4 of 1985 claiming his as tenant under her and prayed for eviction of the petitioner no. 2. The petitioner no. 2 has contested the suit as defendant by filing written statement. The petitioner no. 2 thereafter filed an application for return of the plaint of the suit on the ground that the claim of opposite party no. 2 being disputed on proof or disproof of title. The application was rejected on 2.9.89. The petitioner no. 2 then filed Civil Revision No. 1072 of 1989 and the rule was discharged on 7.1.93. The petitioner no. 2 then filed Civil Petition for leave to Appeal No. 91 of 1993 before the Appellate Division which was dismissed on 20.5.93.

4. Thereafter the petitioner No. 1 asked the petitioner no. 2 to return back her property and the latter returned the property on 21.6.93 and since then the petitioner no. 1 is owning and possessing the suit land by living in some part and through her bharatia. Then the petitioner no. 1 filed an application in S.C.C. suit no. 4 of 1985 under Order 1 Rule 10 C.P.C. for being added as party but the prayer was rejected. Thereafter the petitioner no. 1 instituted Other Class Suit No. 54 of 1992 in the Court of Senior Assistant Judge. Sirajganj Sadar for declaration that the judgment dated 26.9.95 passed in Other Suit no. 103 of 1995 and the judgment dated 22.12.80 passed in O.C. Suit No. 645 of 1978 are not binding upon her and the suit is now pending.

5. Thereafter the petitioner No. 1 and 2 filed Misc. Case No. 45 of 1994 before the learned District Judge. Sirajganj for withdrawal S.C.C. Suit No. 4 of 1985 from the Court of Assistant Judge Sirajganj Sadar and for hearing of the same analogously with Other Class Suit No. 54 of 1993 pending before the Senior Assistant Judge Sirajganj Sadar filed by the petitioner no. 2 but the prayer was rejected by the impugned judgment and order No. 16 dated 19.5.96.

6. Being aggrieved the petitioners moved this court and obtained the present rule.

7. It is undisputed that the suit property was requisitioned by the District Administration. Pabna in Requisition Case no. 23 of 1960 and the Requisition Case was started in the names of original owners. It is also undisputed that the petitioner no. 2 Md. Jalaluddin Sarker was inducted in the disputed property by the District Administration Pabna as allottee of the Government.

8. The case of the opposite party is that the opposite party no. 1 got the suit property from the original owner by way of pattan and ultimately instituted O.C. Suit No. 103 of 1975 and got a decree in her favour. Later on she transferred the suit land to the opposite party no. 2 and delivered possession and opposite party no. 2 also subsequently instituted O.C. Suit No. 645 of 1978 in the Court of Munsif, Sirajganj for declaration of her title. The present opposite party no. 2 made prayer for being added as defendant in the suit but the prayer was rejected on the ground that admittedly the present petitioner no. 2 was an allottee of the Government in respect of the suit property. Civil Revision No. 1072 of 1989 brought by the present petitioner against the present opposite party no. 2 and others before this Court was rejected with following observations:-

"There is no dispute that the Government itself made over possession of the property after its derequisition recognising the plaintiff as its title holder. The defendant has no explanation whatsoever as to how in such circumstances he could in how deny the plaintiffs locus standi to claim rent from the defendant having stepped into the shoes of the Government. It is now well settled that in case the tenant sets up a claim of title in himself he should first surrender possession of the property to the person from whom he had taken it and that mere non-payment of rent cannot be interpreted as inexistence of the tenancy."

9. It was further observed that it is clear that entering into possession as an allottee from Government that present petitioner cannot set up independent title on the basis of some exchange deed.

10. In Civil Petition for leave to Appeal No. 91 of 1993 brought by the present petitioner no. 2 against present opposite party no. 2 our Appellate Division held as under:-

"Because the defendant entered into the premises as an allottee of the Government and as such he is not entitled to deny the title of the plaintiff so long he remains in possession in the capacity as tenant under the Government who made over possession to the plaintiff recognizing the title of the plaintiff in the suit property."

11. Thus it is clear that the claim of the petitioner no. 2 that he got the suit property by way of exchange from the petitioner no. 1 and his claim of title on the basis of the said exchange were not considered and it was held, that he should first surrender possession to the plaintiff and then set up his claim of title.

12. The case of the petitioner no. 1 is that when the claim of the petitioner no. 2 was not accepted up to the Appellate Division of this Court the petitioner no. 1 got back the suit land from petitioner no. 2 on cancellation of the earlier exchange deed between them and instituted Other Class Suit no. 54 of 1993 in the Court of Senior Assistant Judge, Sirajganj Sadar against the present opposite party no. 2 and others for a declaration that the decrees passed in Other Class suit No. 103 of 1975 and Other Class Suit No. 645 of 1978 are illegal void without jurisdiction and not binding upon her. During pendency of the suit the petitioner no. 1 filed a petition dated 19.6.96 for withdrawal of S.C.C. Suit no. 4 of 1985 from the Court of Assistant Judge. Sirajganj Sadar filed by the opposite party no. 1 and hearing of the same analogously with Other Class Suit no. 54 of 1993 pending before the Senior Assistant Judge. Sirajganj Sadar filed by the present petitioner no. 1. The learned District Judge by the impugned Judgment and order rejected the prayer on the grounds inter alia that the S.C.C. Suit No. 4 of 1985 was instituted prior to Other Class suit No. 54 of 1993 and the latter suit was at the stage of return of service of summons.

13. Mr. Khorshed Alam Khan the learned Advocate appearing for the opposite party submits that in S.C.C. suit No. 4 of 1985 one witness has already been examined and cross-examined but Other Class suit no. 54 of 1993 is at the stage of service of summons upon the defendants and it will take a long time to made that suit ready for hearing. The learned District Judge observed that the petitioner in Other Class suit no. 54 of 1993 will have no difficulty in getting relief in accordance with law of both the suits are not at all heard analogously. It was further observed that on the plea of complicated question of title and an analogous trial the disposal of S.C.C. Suit No. 4 of 1985 cannot be further delayed. The learned Advocate for the opposite party further submits that there is also no specific provision in the Code of Civil Procedure for consolidation of suits for holding analogous trial but the Court exercises its inherent power in the interest of justice for avoiding multiplicity of litigations. He further submits that for analogous trial of two suits the principle is that the parties in both the suits and the subject-matter of the suits and the issues involved in the two suits must be the same but in the instant case the parties in both the suits are not the same and the issues involved are the same. Accordingly the leaned District Judge has rightly rejected the prayer.

14. Mrs. Masuma Akhtar, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner submits that it is true that the claim of the petitioner no. 2 Jamaluddin Sarker that he got the suit property by way of exchange from petitioner No. 1 was not accepted up to the Appellate Division and the petitioner no. 2 was directed to first surrender the possession of the property in favour of the defendant-opposite party no. 2 and then to set up his claim of title. She further submits that thereafter the petitioner. No. 1 got back the property by cancellation of the deed of exchange from petitioner no. 2 and filed Other Class Suit no. 54 of 1993 and also filed a petition on 19.6.95 before the learned District Judge for withdrawal of S.C.C. Suit No. 4 of 1985 from the Court of Assistant Judge Sadar Sirajganj for analogous trial with Other Class suit No. 54 of 1993 pending before the Senior Assistant Judge Sadar Sirajganj. But she found it difficult to assail the impugned order of the learned District Judge.

<u>15. Having regard to the facts and circumstances of the case, materials on record and in the light of my above discussion I hold that since the parties and the issue involved in the two suits are not the same the prayer for holding analogous trial of both the suits was rightly rejected by the learned District Judge and this Court has nothing to interfere with.</u>

The Rule is accordingly discharged without any order as to costs. The stay order dated 14.8.96 granted by this Court is hereby vacated.

End.
