Md. Ismailuddin Sarkar, J. This Rule at the instance of the plaintiffs is directed against the judgment and order dated 29-12-83 passed by the Munsif Upazills Kotwali para, Faridpur in Misc. case No.37 of 1983 allowing an application under order 9 Rule 13 C.P.C. setting aside the exparte decree dated 9-3-83.

2. The petitioners have filed Title suit No. 115 of 1974 in the Court of Munsif Gopalganj against the opposite party and others for a declaration of their title and confirmation of possession in respect of the suit land and the said suit was decreed exparte of 9-3-82. Thereafter the opposite party who was defendant No.3 in the suit filed on application under order 9 Rule 13 C.P.C. which was registered as Misc. case no.37 of 1983 for seating aside the exparte decree on the ground inter alia that no summons or registered letter was served upon him and that the services return has been shown as duly served in collusion with the process server. The opposite party came to know about the exparte decree on 30-3-83 when petitioner No.1 disclosed about the exparte decree. Thereafter the opposite party made a search in the court and got information about the date of his knowledge.

3. The plaintiff petitioner No.1 contested the application denying the material allegation made in the application and contending inter alia that the summons and the registered letter was duly served upon the defendants and that the application is barred by limitation. The learned Munsif allowed the application on condition of payment of costs of Tk. 50/- to the plaintiffs. Hence this revisional application by the plaintiffs.

<u>4. Mr. Shahid Alam, the learned Advocate appearing in support of the rule contends that the learned Munsif compared the signature of the opposite party in the service return with his, signatures take in the courts and found that both the signatures tally. The learned Munsif also observed that the opposite party and defendant No. 4 reside in the same homestead and as such the opposite party should have knowledge about the exparte-decree earlier than the date mentioned by him. Yet the learned Munsif allowed the Misc. case being of the opinion that the opposite party should get a chance to contest the original suit to prove his title to the suit land. According to Mr. Alam, the learned Munsif virtually found that summons was duly served upon the opposite party and as such the learned Munsif erred in law in allowing an application under order 9. Rule 13 C.P.C. and setting aside the exparte decree. Mr. Bazlur Rahman Talukdar, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the opposite party, on the other hand submits that the opposite party as P.W. 1 stated that he had no knowledge of the original suit and that no summons was served upon him. He has also examined as P.W. 2 Dhirendra Nath Barrio who has stated that he did not sign the alleged service return. On the other hand, the plaintiff opposite party adduced no evidence to prove that summons was duly served upon the opposite party. According to Mr. Talukdar the learned Munsif should have found on the evidence on record that no summons was served upon the opposite party. This being a case of non-service of summons the learned Munsif was justified in setting aside the exparte decree. In support of his contention Mr. Talukdar has referred to the decision of the Appellate Division in the case of Md. Abdur Rashid and another V. Abdul Barik and another reported in 1984 B.L.D). (A.D.) 83.</u>

<u>5. It appears that although the learned Munsif compared the signature in the service return with the signature of P.W. 1 taken in the court he has not come to a definite finding that there was service of summons. On the other hand P.W. 1 stated that there was no service of summons upon him and that he had no knowledge of the original suit prior to the date of his knowledge as given in his application under order 9. Rule 13 C.P.C. P.W. 2 Dhirerndra Nath Barui has also stated that he did not sing the service return Ext.1 as witness. As regards the evidence adduced on behalf of the plaintiffs opposite parties, the learned Munsif found "The O.P. did not take any step to prove the service retain by adducing any evidence. O.P.1 as O.P.W. 1 has told that the process server of Ext.1 is dead. He could bring any other process server who knows the handwriting of Abdus Sattar who served the summons Ext. 1" Thus It appears that the plaintiffs opposite parties failed to prove by adducing cogent evidence that summons of the original suit was served upon opposite party defendant No.3. In that view of the matter, the irresistible conclusion is that there was no service of summons upon defendant No.3 and as such the exparte decree is liable to be set aside. In view of the decision of the Appellate Division referred to above that under order 9. Rule 13 C.P.C. if summons is not Duly served on the defendants that in a good ground for setting aside the exparte decree because service of summons is an essential condition which must be satisfied before the court can proceed to an exparte decree and when a party satisfies the court that summons were not duly served upon him the Court is bound to set aside the exparte decree. In such a case the question of knowledge is not at all relevant and the expert decree will be set aside even if the defendant had knowledge of the institution of the suit. In view of the finding that there was no service of summons the contention of Mr. Shahid Alam that the learned Munsif was wrong in allowing the application on compassionate ground to give a chance to the defendant to contest the suit need not be considered. In that view of the matter, the Rule is discharged without any order as to costs.</u>

<u>The learned Munsif is directed to dispose of the suit expeditiously.</u>

End.

lawyer: Mashi-ul-Islam, Advocate ----- for the petitioner Prasanta Kumar Bose with Mansur Habib, Advocates for opposite party Nos. 1 and 2.
parties:
Mokbul Hussain and Others
Vs.
Akhil Kumar Shaha and Others
full_judgment:
Muhammad Abdul Wahab, J:--This Rule at the instance of defendant is directed against the judgment and decree dated 14-12-81 passed by the learned Additional District Judge, Court Bogra in Other Class Appeal No.19 of 1981 reversing those of the learned Munsif, 2nd Court, Bogra in Other Class Suit No.163 of 1978.

2. The case of the plaintiff, in brief, is that the jote appertaining to C.S. Khatian No.89 of mouza Pali Moheshpur under P.S. Dhupchachia District Bogra measuring 1.90 decimals originally belonged to Rajmohon Shaha and Ramkumar Shaha in equal share. That Rajmohan Shaha died leaving 4 sons Mohabharat Shahs, Bhagabat Chandra Shaha, Basanta Kumar Shaha, Gakul Chandra Shaha as his heirs. That Mohabharat Shaha died leaving one son Norendra Nath Shaha who afterwards died issueless and the aforesaid Basonta Kumar Shaha and Gokul Chandra Shaba also died issueless. That Bhagabat Chandra Shaha died leaving plaintiff No. 2 as his only son and as such he acquired /8/- annas share in the suit jote. That Ramkumar Shaha died leaving 2 sons Keshab Chanda and Okhoy Kumar Shaha. That Keshab Chandra Shaha died leaving 4 sons, Shiris Chandra, Khithish Chandra Shaha. Jogoballav Shaha, and Radhaballav Shaha and being in possession over their /4/- annas share sold to pro-defdt. Nos. 7-11 by registered kabalas. That Akhoy Kumar Shaha died leaving one son puff. No.1 as his heir and as such the plaintiffs and pro-defdts are in a ejmali possession over the suit jote. That in M.R.R. the suit jote have been

recorded in the name of Rajmohon Shaha, Bhagabat Chandra Shaha, Mohabharat Chandra Shaha, Gokul Chandra Shaba, Keshab Chandra Shaha, Rajmohon Shaha, Basanta Kumar Shaha, Akhoy Kumar Shaha along with pro-defdt. Nos. 7-11. That the said M.R.R. record is wrong since the same has been prepared in the name of their predecessor-in-interest who died long ago. That the pro-defdt. No.10 used to look after the suit jote from the time of their predecessor-in-interest and being in possession of all papers managed to start the certificate Case No.697-13/60-61 against the dead persons and has auction purchased the same in the name of his sons and nephews the defdt. Nos: 2-6 by suppressing all the notices in collusion with the staff. That no delivery of possession took place nor they were aware about the alleged certificate sale but first came to know front one Nader Mondal who alleged to have reported him (the plaintiff No.1) about their (defdt. No. 2-6) alleged auction purchase on 31-1-78 A.D. and being aware they have come to know in details on 4-2-78 A.D. after having obtained certified copy of the said certificate case. Hence the plaintiff filed this suit.

3. The defendant Nos. 2-6 contested the suit by filing a joint written statement denying all the allegations of the plaintiffs. They have challenged the case of the plaintiffs on all material points and alleged that the suit is hit by section 42 of the S.R. Act. Their case is total denial and inter alia case is that the defdt. No. 7-11 purchased '47 decimals by registered kabalas from the heirs of Keshab Chandra Kundu and being in ejmali possession with other co-sharers the suit jote was put to auction in certificate Case No. 697-B/60-61 for arrears of rent and that they have been possessing the suit jote since getting delivery from court on/from 30-12-62 A.D. That since then they are paying rent after mutating the jama. That the plaintiffs or the certificate debtors were all along aware about the same but did not object. That they have received compensation for acquisition of a portion of the suit jote for Bogra Snatehar road in Misc. Case 29-G/67. That they have also sold some portion of the suit jote to Osman Fakir and others wherein the said purchasers are carrying out their business by erecting shops. That they use the water of the suit tank for the purpose of irrigation and also rearing up fishes and are in possession of the banks of the said tank by planting various trees.

4. The defendant Nos. 7-8 admit the case of the plffs in toto and opposed the case of the defdt. Nos. 2-6 whereas the defdt. Nos. 15, 17, 18, 20, 23, 27 and 30 supported the case of the defdt. Nos. 2-6 in toto.

5. The learned Munsif after considering the facts, circumstances and evidence on records dismissed the suit.

6. On appeal the learned Additional District Judge considering the circumstances and evidence on record allowed the appeal and set aside the judgment and decree of the learned Munsif.

7. The defendant petitioner obtained this rule from this court on 7-6-82.

<u>8. Mr. Masih-Ul-Islam the learned Advocate for the petitioners submits that the suit is not maintainable in its present form and it is hit by Section 42 of the Specific Relief Act. He has cited the following decisions in support of his contention, 7 DLR 50, 13 DLR 70, and 30 DLR 116. It is true that the prayer in the plaint was for simple declaration to the effect that the judgment of the certificate proceeding bearing No, 697-B/60-61 and the sale held thereunder is illegal, collusive, fraudulent and is not binding upon the plaintiffs. The plaintiff did not ask for recovery of possession of the land. In 13 DLR 70 in the case of Syed Ahmed V. Prafulla Kumar Dey and ors. His lordship Mr. Justice B.A. Siddiky has held that it is not the case of the plaintiff that they are in possession of the suit lands, on the other hand it is not denied by them that the possession was taken by auction purchaser in the land. In these circumstances plaintiff's suit must fail under Section 42 of the Specific Relief Act inasuch as being out of possession he has not asked for recovery of possession as a consequential relief. Even in a case when the defendants plead of his having taken symbolical possession or that there is evidence of the defendant having taken symbolical possession, the plaintiff must pray for recovery of possession in a suit for declaration of his title otherwise the suit will be hit by Section 42 of the Specific Relief Act. But in the instant case the plaintiffs did not file this suit for declaration of their title. They have prayed for simple declaration to the effect that the judgment of the certificate proceeding bearing No. 697-B/60-61 of Bogra District and sale held thereunder is illegal, collusive, fraudulent and is not binding upon the plaintiffs. So the prayer for consequential relief is not required in the instant case. So the suit will be not hit by section 42 of the Specific Relief Act. The learned Advocate further submits that the suit is barred under section 36 of the Public Demand Recovery Act. Under that section the plaintiff must file his suit within one year from the date of the delivery of possession. The provision of section 36 of the Act barred to the effect that the sale of immovable property in execution of a certificate shall not be held to be void that the notices required to section 7 has not been served but it provides that, the plaintiff to launch a suit in a civil court either to recover possession of the property or set aside the sale on the ground of substcutial injury sustained by him by reason of irregularity of non service of notice. Accordingly the aggrieved party then an filed the suit either for recovery of possession or (setting aside sale of property on proof of substantial injury sustained by reason of irregularity of non service of notice. A sale held without certificate proceeding is not void merely on the ground of non-service of notice under Section 7 of the P.D.R Act. It is only voidable for that his suit must be brought for setting aside sale within one year from the date of the delivery of possession under Section 36. of the Act. But (when a sale has been brought about by means of fraud, Proviso (a), to Section 36 of the P.D.R. Act will not be attracte & the pltfl: will be competent to take advantage of section 18 of the limitation Act, in computing the time for bringing his suit. The learned Advocate further submits that the suit is also hit by section 37 of the PDR Act. I find that there is no sub-stance in the contention of the learned Advocate for the petitioner. Section 37 of the P.D.R. Act provides for general bar to the jurisdiction of the Civil Court and says that every question arising between the certificate-holder and the certificate-debtor or their representatives relating to the execution, discharge or satisfaction of a certificate or relating to confirmation or setting aside of sale shall be determined not by suit, but by order of certificate Officer. However, the proviso to this section provides that where fraud is alleged a suit in the Civil Court may be instituted. So the general jurisdiction of the Civil Court to entertain suits of Civil nature on the ground of fraud is not barred. The learned Advocate further submits that the suit is also hit by Article 142 and 144 of the Limitation Act. Article 142 and 144 of the Act provides the party should Jill the suit within 12 years from the date of dispossession of the immovable property but in the instant case the plaintiff filed the suit after 17 years. So the suit is barred under Article 142 and 144 of the limitation\Act. (IX of 1908). Though it is true but the principle of Limitation of article 142 and 144 of the Limitation Act will not be applicable to the instant case. Because in case of fraud, the pltff: will be competent to take advantage of Section 18 of the Limitation Act in computing the time for bringing his suit.</u>

9. Mr. Present Kumar Bose, the learned Advocate for the opposite parties submits that the certificate proceedings were against dead person. So this certificate sale is a nullity. He has taken me to the judgment of the learned lower appellate court and found that the learned Additional District Judge found that the Judgment debtors, namely, Bhogobat Chandra Shaha. Mohabharat Chandra Shaha, Basanta Kwnar Shaha and Gokul Chandra Shaha arc all dead persons. The learned Advocate cites 20 BLR 1103 and DLR 1972 Vol. 1176 relevant page 187, 32 DLR 167 (AD) in support of his contention. I have found that there is substance in the contention of the learned Advocate for the opposite parties. The Learned Advocate further submits that if fraud is practiced then there will be no limitation of time to file the suit. In that case the suit may be filed within 3 years from the date of knowledge and in the instant case the plaintiff find the suit within one month of the date of knowledge. There is substance in the contention of the learned Advocate for the opposite parties.

10. I have gone through the judgment of the learned lower appellate court and found that the learned Judge discussed all the points of law and facts in details to arrive at a conclusion. I have also found that the learned lower appellate court has not committed any error of law apparent on the face of the record. For discussions and the reasons stated above, I am not inclined to interfere with the judgment and decree of the learned lower appellate court.

In the result the Rule is discharged without any order as to costs.

Send down the lower courts records at once.

End.

lawyer: Mr. S.K. Sinha with Mr. Md. Shafiqur Rahman, Advocate ------ For the petitioner.
parties:
Al-Helal Rice Mills Ltd ------ Petitioner
Vs.
Bangladesh Shilpa Rin Sangsta ------Respondent
full_judgment:
A M Mahmudur Rahman J: The petitioner is a private Ltd. company. In 1978 the Department of Food proposed to the Managing Director of the company whether the company is desirous of obtaining loan to establish an automatic rice mill for milling of paddy to be supplied by the said Department and in case it so desire they would make necessary arrangements for the fund from Asian Development Bank. The petitioner applied for such fund. Being satisfied with the application on Inquiry it accepted the scheme of the petitioner for obtaining such loan and the respondent Sangstha sanctioned initially loan for U.S.$ 1,33,000/- for supply of the machinery for the petitioner M/s. Al-Helal Automatic Rice Mill Ltd. and the Sangstha selected Indian suppliers and the money sanctioned was in yen at 2,91,83,486 equivalent to Indian Currency Rs. 9,80,000/-Machinery and equipment were sent to Bangladesh and the petitioner released the same. Supplied machinery fell short of the required one, petitioner repeatedly made claim to the B.S.R.S for direction to the supplier to replace the wanting parts of the machinery. Further the quality of the machinery, were defective and inferior one and was in terms of tender. Inspite of the repeated demand of the petitioner to the respondent to make book loss for its failure. The petitioner had to renovate the same at his own cost. The result was the mill could not be run in a full swing and ultimately had to stop its functioning for such defective machineries. In such a situation the respondent Bangladesh Shilpa Rin Snagsta made demand to repay the loan with interest. The petitioner replied that for no fault of it mill could not be run and it did not violate any terms of loan agreement. The petitioner further prayed for exemption of interest and the privilege of installment for payment of the loan. However, the petitioner paid Tk. 8,88,255/- by installments. Even after acceptance of such payment the respondent filed Certificate Case No. 127/90 for recovery of Tk. 2.619 Million in local currency Tk. 0.5000 million with interest. The petitioner instituted of Title Suit No. 44/90 in the Court of Subordinate Judge, Moulvibazar for declaration that Certificate case filed malafide and it was void. The suit was contested by the respondent. During the trial one Mr. Khalid Hossain, Principal Officer of Bangladesh Shilpa Rin Shansta deposed admitting that Bangladesh Shilpa Rin Sangsta imported machineries and the petitioner has, no choice to purchase the machinery and the loan was paid in yen as noted above. The learned Subordinate Judge decreed the suit with the finding that the claim for recovery of the loan amount "is in serious dispute". In the meantime after the decree was made respondent instituted Miscellaneous Case No. 260/92 in 2 Artha Rin Adalat, Dhaka under section 33 of the Bangladesh Shilpa Sangstha Order, 1972 (P.O. 128/72) claiming for a decree of Tk. 3,114/- Million with interest thereon. The petitioner, on the other hand, instituted Title Suit No. 5/94 in the 1st Court of Subordinate Judge, Moulvibazar claiming damage of Tk. 1,00,00,000/- During pendency of the suits the Bangladesh Shilpa Rin Sangstha, the respondent, advertised for sale of the property for recovery of the loan amount. The dispute raised ultimately went before the Appellate Division on the question of injunction. Appellate Division by its order dated 4.6.97 granted leave stayed the operation of the injunction holding that High Court Division failed to consider the bar provided in Article 34 of the aforesaid Order in granting injunction. It further held that Article 34 is a provision of special law and shall prevail over general law. And held that the trial court in granting temporary injunction acted contrary to the scheme of the legislation which is a special one meaning the Bangladesh Shilpa Rin Sangsta Order, 1972.

2. The questions that fall our determination for disposal of this application are whether, as contended by Mr. Sinha, in a case of disputed demand can there be application of section 34 of the Order for sale of the property to recover the amount under demand. Secondly, whether prior to taking possession of the mill itself by the respondent such advertisement for direct sale under section 34 can be made. Thirdly, whether the officer of the respondent having had deposed before the Civil Court and such deposition giving rise to a dispute regarding the amount to be recovered by instituting a civil suit issuance of notice under section 34 of the Order can be maintained in law. Mr. Sinha in continuation of his contention has taken us through the provision of section 34 of the Order and also cited a decision in the case of New Ideal Engineering Works Vs. Bangladesh Shilpa Rin Sangsta, 42 DLR 221(AD).

Section 34 of the Order is:

"Where any industrial concern which is under a liability to the Sangstha under an agreement made any default in payment or otherwise fails to comply with the terms of its agreement with the Sangstha, the Sangstha may not-withstanding anything contained in Article 33 take over the management and administration of the industrial concern, and may sell or realise any property pledged, mortgaged, hypothecated or assigned by the industrial concern to secure its liability to the Sangstha."

<u>3. A careful reading of the aforesaid provisions of law leads us to hold that in spite of institution of a suit under section 33 of the Order a proceeding for recovery of the amount by Bangladesh Shilpa Rin Sangstha re-course to section 34 can be had for direct sale of the property. The learned Advocate could not place before us from the Order that it also provides for an ouster clause in the event of taking parallel action for realising of the demand by the Sangstha itself in Civil Court or before any other authority nor we could find such ouster clause. On the other hand, for the expressions used in section 34 "Notwithstanding anything contained in Article 33", we find no want of authority in publishing the impugned advertisement on the part of the Respondent-Sangstha. Reference to section 33 indicates that the respondent Sangstha can institute a proceeding for the reliefs, namely, sale of the property pledged etc transfer of management and administration, and order for injunction restraining the industrial concern from removing the premise of the said industrial concern without permission of the Sangstha or from destroying, transferring etc. and or for payment of loan. Relying upon the decision referred to above the question posed by Mr. Sinha answer is obtained in paragraph 6 of the report which does not support his contention rather it demolished his contention. At page 222 of the report is held:</u>

<u>“as to the first contention it was found that the Articles 33 and 34 of the Order are exclusive of each other”</u>

<u>Provision of section 34 of the Order has been much more fortified by the observation quoted above. The point having had been act at rest by the aforesaid observation of the Appellate Division we do not find any difficult to hold that the impugned notification as advertised under section 34 of the Order cannot be issued for the reason of the provision of Section 33 of the Order and as such we hold that the advertisement has been made with lawful authority. Lastly, it remains for us to speak on the disputed amount of money. In order to obtain a relief under Article 102 of the Constitution. The petitioner should come with an undisputed claim to invoke our power under Article 102 of the Constitution. Therefore, the petition also fails on the ground of disputed amount sought to be recovered by civil court's decree. For the aforesaid reasons we find no substance in this petition. In the result, we reject limine with cost of Tk. 3,000/- (Three thousand) only.</u>

End.

caseno:
Civil Revision No. 305 of 2003
With
Civil Revision No. 974 of 2003
lawyer:
Mr. Md. Fazlul Karim with Mr. H.N. Nondy and Mr. Kh. Aminul Haque, Advocates ----- for the petitioner of Cr. No. 305/2003 and opposite party of C.R. No. 974/2003
Mr. A.J. Mohammad Ali with Mr. Sultan Mahmud & Ms. Bilkis Jahan, Advocates ----- for the Opposite parties of Civil Rev. No. 305/2003 and petitioner of Civil Revision No. 974/2003
parties:
Md. Shahjahan Miah
Vs.
Md. Mustaque Hossain and another
full_judgment:
Md. Abdul Aziz, J:- In Civil Revision No. 305/2003 Rule was issued at the instance of Md. Shahjahan Miah, calling upon the opposite parties to show cause as to why the order dated 28.11.2002 passed by the learned Assistant Judge, 3rd Court, Dhaka in Miscellaneous Case No. 6/2002 should not be set aside.

2. In Civil Revision No. 974 of 2003 Rule was issued at the instance of Md. Mustaque Hossain, upon the opposite party No. 1 Md. Shahjahan Mia to show cause as to why the order dated 4.3.2003 passed by the learned Assistant Judge, 3rd Court, Dhaka in Title Execution Case No. 2 of 2002 should not be set aside.

3. Both the Rules are taken up for hearing together pursuant to order passed in Civil Revision No. 974/2003 at the time of issuing Rule and are heard and disposed of accordingly by this judgment.

4. Facts relevant for disposal of Civil Re-vision No. 305/2003, in short, is that the petitioner, Md. Shahjahan Miah instituted S.C.C. Suit no. 3/1993 on 4.2.1993 which was re numbered as S.C.C. Suit no. 3/1997 against the opposite parties Md. Mostaque Hosain and Md. Abdul Hye for evicting them as defaulter from the Suit shop who were his monthly tenants vide agreement dated 13.4.1988 renewed by agreement dated 19.5.1981 AD. The opposite parties are two full brothers and had been running business in the suit shop.

5. Opposite party No. 2 Md. Abdul Hye who was defendant No. 1 in the suit contested the suit by filing written statements. The learned Assistant Judge, 2nd Court, Dhaka decreed the suit against him on contest and ex parte against opposite party no. 1 Md. Mustaque Hossain who was defendant No. 2 in the suit vide it's judgment dated 17.11.1997. The opposite party no. 2 filed C.R. case No. 377/1998 under section 25 of Small Causes Courts Act before the High Court Division against the aforesaid judgment and decree and a single Bench of the High Court Division by its judgment and order dated 3.11.98 sent the case back on remand to the trial court for re-trial making the rule absolute reversing the judgment and decree of the trial court. The petitioner filed a Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 662/1999 before the Appellate Division against the aforesaid judgment and order of the High Court Division impleading both the defendant opposite parties. The Appeal No. 105/1999 arose which was allowed on contest vide judgment dated 24.10.2000. The opposite party No. 2 made Civil Review Petition bearing No. 64/2001 against the same which was also rejected by the Appellate Division vide its order dated 29.4.02. In the meantime the opposite party No. 1 Md. Mostaque Hossain, who was defendant no. 2 in the suit started Miscellaneous Case No. 85 of 1997 renumbered as Miscellaneous Case No. 6 of 2002 on an application field by him under order 9, rule 13 of the Code for setting aside the ex parte decree passed on 17.11.97 against him. The petitioner after disposal of the aforesaid Civil Appeal No. 105/99 and Review No. 64/2001 by the Appellate Division started title Execution Case No. 2 of 2001 on 1.3.01 in the 3rd Court of Assistant Judge, Dhaka which was re numbered as Execution Case No. 2/2002 on transfer. The opposite party no. 1 obtained an order dated 20.3.02 passed in Miscellaneous Case No. 85/97 staying the proceeding of aforesaid Execution Case. The petitioner challenged the said order before the High Court Division in C.R. Case No. 1825/2002 and obtained a rule along with an order of stay of the said order. The rule was made absolute on 22.5.02 and the said impugned order dated 20.3.02 staying the proceeding of Execution 'Case was set aside Opposite party no. 1 Md. Mostaque Hossain filed Civil Miscellaneous Petition No. 326/02 in the Appellate Division and obtained an order of stay against the judgment and order dated 22.5.02 passed by the High Court Division and thereafter filed a regular petition for Leave to Appeal bearing no 1064/02 and the same was dismissed on 1.12.02. In the meantime the learned Assistant Judge, 3rd Court, Dhaka by its impugned judgment and order passed on 28.11.02 allowed the aforesaid Miscellaneous Case no. 6/02 and restored the S.C.C. Suit no. 3/97 setting aside the judgment and decree passed ex parte on 17.11.97 against the opposite party no. 1. Hence this rule at the instance of the plaintiff petitioner Md. Shahajahan Miah.

6. The facts of Civil Revision No. 974/03 are similar to the facts of C.R. No. 305 of 2003 as stated above. The petitioner stated that he and defendant opposite party No. 2 took lease of the suit shop from opposite party No. 1 on the basis of lease agreement dated 19.3.81 paying a salami of Tk. 3,00,000/- and the two shop rooms were converted and amalgamated into one room and a new lease deed was executed on 13.4.88 between the parties. The petitioner and the opposite party No. 2 had been carrying on business in the said shop. The opposite party No. 1 filed S.S.C. suit No. 3/97 against them for their eviction and got decree dated 17.11.97 on contest against opposite party no. 2 and ex parte against the petitioner. The opposite party No. 2 Md. Abdul Hye fought unsuccessfully against the said decree upto appellate Division. The petitioner was also a party in the aforesaid proceedings. Thereafter on the application of the plaintiff opposite party no. 1 under section 151 of the code filed on 18.2.03 the learned Assistant Judge, 3rd Court, Dhaka vide its impugned order dated 4.3.03 directed to proceed with the execution of decree in title Execution case No. 2/02. Hence this Rules.

7. Perused the applications, the impugned judgments and orders and heard the learned Advocates of both the sides. From the facts of both the rules it appears that the petitioner in Civil Revision No. 305/03 and opposite party no. 1 in Civil Revision No. 305/03 and opposite party no. 1 in Civil Revision No. 974/03 as plaintiff instituted S.C.C. Suit No. 3/93 re numbered as S.C.C. Suit no. 3/97 for ejectment being deaulter against the opposite party no. 1 Md. Mustaque Hossain and opposite party no.  2 Md. Abdul Hye in Civil Revision No. 305/03 who are petitioner and opposite party no. 2 respectively in Civil Revision No. 974/03. Admittedly they are full brothers and joint tenants in respect of the suit premises. Originally they took lease on rent of two rooms vide agreement dated 19.3.81 from the plaintiff and thereafter on converting and amalgamation of said two rooms into one room they continued in possession there of vide agreement of lease dated 13.4.88 till the S.C.C. suit was filed against them for their ejectment. This is also admitted that the two brothers used to run the business in the same shop and one of the brothers Md. Abdul Hye, who is opposite party no. 2 in both the rules, contested the suit by filing written statements and the suit was decreed on contest against him and ex parte against other brother Md. Mustaque Hossain who is opposite party no. 1 in Civil Revision No. 305/03 and petitioner in Civil Revision No. 974/03. The said decree was upheld up to the Appellate Division on contest. Md. Mustaque Hossain in C.R. 974/03 who was defendant no. 2 in S.C.C. Suit no. 3/93 filed an application under order 9 rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure against the ex parte decree in Miscellaneous Case No. 85/1997 re numbered as Miscellaneous Case No. 6/02 for setting aside the ex parte decree which was allowed by the trial court vide impugned order dated 28.11.02 against which Civil Revision No. 305/03 arose.

8. Provisions of order 9, rule 13 of the C.P.C. are as follows:

13 In any case in which a decree is passed ex parte against a defendant he may apply to the court by which the decree was passed for an order to set it aside, and if he satisfies the Court that the summons was not duly served, or that he was prevented by any sufficient cause from appearing when the suit was called on for hearing the court shall make and order setting aside the decree as against him upon such terms as to costs, payment into court or otherwise as it thinks fit, and shall appoint a day for proceeding with the suit.

Provided that where the decree is of such a nature that it cannot be set aside as against such defendant only it may be set aside as against all or any of the other defendants also.

9. Referring the above provision Mr. Fazlul Karim, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner in Civil Revision No. 305/03 submitted that the order of the trial court dated 4.9.93 passed in the suit shows that the summons have been satisfactorily served upon the (both) defendants. He also submitted that the opposite party no. 1 has not also been able to show that he was prevented by sufficient cause from appearing when the suit was called on for hearing. The opposite party No. 1 having thus failed to satisfy the court that the summons was not duly served upon him nor he was prevented by any sufficient cause from appearing when the suit was called on for hearing the impugned order is liable to be set aside, Mr. Karim added. He further submitted that the impugned order is neither an objective order nor a speaking order and does not base on evidence. He continued that the trial court neither gave any finding nor an reason whatsoever for setting aside the ex parte decree and as such the impugned order is also liable to be set aside. He also submitted referring the protracted proceedings up to the Appellate Division that the decree passed in S.C.C. Suit against the contesting brother, namely, Md. Abdul Hye having been upheld. The ex parte decree passed against the other brother Md. Mustaque Hossain, the opposite party no. 1 has been merged with the same inasmuch as the decree is indivisible as both the brothers are joint tenants, jointly possess the rented shop and run their business there. Mr. Karim lastly contended that the trial court failed to exercise its jurisdiction while allowing the case in not finding that the miscellaneous case was not maintainable as any security as required under section 17(1) of the Small Cause Courts Act was given by the opposite party No. 1.

10. Mr. Md. Fazlul Karim, the learned Advocate appearing for the plaintiff opposite party no. 1 in Civil Revision No. 974/2003 contended that the executing court has rightly passed the impugned order directing to proceed with the execution case pursuant to the judgment and order passed by the Appellate Division and as such the rule is liable to be discharged with costs. Mr. Karim also submits that the defendant in S.C.C. Suit no. 3/97 being the opposite parties in Civil Revision No. 305/03 are two full brothers who took lease of the shop jointly as co tenant an have been running the business in the same shop together. The decree dated 17.11.97 passed in S.C.C. suit No. 3/97 is indivisible and binding on both the defendants. Mr. Karim has referred the cases of Mono Mohan Kundu Vs. Nripendra Nath Nandi and others reported in AIR 1937 (Cal) 548 and also the case of Abdul Jalil Bhuiyan and ors. Vs. Majibar Nessa and others reported in 12 DLR (1960) 581.

11. Mr. A.J. Mohammad Ali, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the opposite parties in Civil Revision No. 305/03 as well as for the petitioner in Civil Revision No. 974/03 found difficult to controvert the submissions of Mr. Karim in the facts and circumstances of the case. He also admitted the joint tenancy, joint possession and running their business in the same suit shop Mr. Ali the learned Advocate appearing for the opposite party nos. 1 and 2 in Civil Revision No. 305/03 however controverted the submissions made by the learned advocate appearing for the petitioner contending that the learned Assistant Judge has rightly and properly passed the impugned order allowing the miscellaneous case and restoring the S.C.C. Suit no. 3/97 setting aside the ex parte decree dated 17.11.97. He further submits that as the Opposite Party No. 1 did not contest the suit and the decree having been passed ex parte against him he had rightly initiated the miscellaneous case filing an application under order 9, rule 13 of the Code for restoring the suit to its original file and number on setting aside the exparte decree and such right has not been taken away in the proceedings fought by opposite party no. 2 up to the Appellate Division. He also submits that the exparte decree dated 17.11.97 has not been merged with the decree upheld by the Appellate Division passed on contest against opposite party no. 2 Appearing for the petitioner in Civil Revision No. 974/2003 he submits that the executing court has illegally passed the impugned order dated 4.3.03 directing to proceed with the execution case without considering that the decree dated 17.11.97 passed ex parte against the petitioner in S.C.C. Suit no. 3/97 has already been set aside and the suit has been restored. Mr. Ali lastly submits that success of the instant rule C.R.974/903 depends upon the fate of Civil Revision No. 305/2003. In support of his submissions Mr. Ali has referred some decisions in cases between Atul Chandra Das Vs. Bhagabati Das and others reported to 18 DLR 1966 81, Makhan Lal Dutta Vs. Joytun Bibi and others reported in 16 DLR 1964 130 Abdur Rashid and another Vs. Abdul Barik and another, reported in 35 DLR (AD) 162 and also reported in 4 BLD (AD) 83.

<u>12. In consideration of the fact and circumstances of the case and on perusal of the impugned order dated 28.11.02 allowing the Miscellaneous case, I find substance in the submission of Mr. Karim that in setting aside an ex parte decree under order 9 rule 13 of the Code, the court must be satisfied that there was no due Service of summons or the petitioner was prevented by any sufficient cause from appearing before the court when the case was called on for hearing. But the learned Assistant Judge in passing the Impugned order dated 28.11.02 gave no finding whatsoever nor any reason justifying setting aside the ex parte decree fulfilling the provisions of rule 13 of order 9 of the C.P.C. as quoted above. On the other hand, order vide order No. 10 dated 4.9.93 passed in S.C.C. suit No. 3/93 shows that the summons were duly served upon the defendants satisfactorily. There is also no finding in the impugned order that the defendant opposite party no. 1 Md. Mustaque Hossain was prevented by any sufficient cause from appearing in court when the suit was called on for hearing. In that view of the matter as none of the essential conditions of rule 13 of order 9 of the Code having been met the trial court committed an error in passing the impugned order setting aside the ex parte decree allowing his application filed under order 9 rule 13 of the said Code and restoring the S.C.C. Suit no. 3/97 resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice and as such the same is liable to be set aside. It is true that an application under order 9, rule 13 of the Code is subgenera’s and is independent and concurrent remedies are available to an aggrieved party having no nexus with an appeal filed against the contested decree or with a review application under order 47 of the Code, but it is equally true that the fate of the application under order 9 rule 13 of the Code is dependent on the compliance and fulfillment of its requirement. But in the instant case there is absolutely no such compliance and hence the decisions referred by Mr. Ali as mentioned above in support of his contention are not applicable in the facts and circumstances of the instant case. More-over, admittedly the suit shop is a single room shop taken lease jointly by both the brothers being defendant nos. 1 and 2 in the suit and had admittedly been possessing by them by running their business in the same shop which conclusively indicates that the decree dated 17.11.97 is indivisible. The decisions in the cases reported in A.I.R. 1937 (Cal) 548 and reported in 12 DLR 581 referred by Mr. Karim supports the same. Nowhere at any stage of the proceeding either before this court or Appellate Division there has been any material on record to show that Md. Mustaque Hossain had any clash of interest with his co tenant brother Md. Abdul Hye. In consideration of the facts, circumstances and materials on record of the case as stated above I am of the opinion that the decree passed in S.C.C. suit no. 3/97 is indivisible and the ex parte decree has been merged with the contested decree upheld by the Appellate Division and the same cannot be set aside on an application under order 9 rule 13 of the code and as such the impugned order dated 28.11.02 challenged in C.R. No. 305/02 is liable to be set aside. The decisions in the case between Mono Mohan Kundu Vs. Nripendra Nath Nandi and others, reported in AIR 1937 (Cal) 548 referred by Mr. Karim which has been elaborately quoted and discussed in the case of Abdul Jalil Bhuiyan and ors. Vs. Majibar Nessa Bibi and others, reported in 12 DLR 581 so I refrain from stating the same here to avoid repetition.</u>

13. In consideration of my above discussions and findings I am of the opinion that the rule in Civil Revision No. 305/2003 has substance and the rule issued in Civil Revision No. 974/2003 has no merit and is liable to be discharged.

14. The conduct of Md. Mustaque Hossain, the petitioner in Civil Revision No. 974/2003 and opposite party no. 1 in Civil Revision No. 305/03 appears mala fide, ill designed and tends to practice fraud consciously upon the court and is deliberate effect of abuse of the process of the court and also tends to cause harassment entailing unnecessary huge cost to Md. Shahjahan Miah, the plaintiff of S.C.C. suit No. 3/1997 who is the petitioner in Civil Revision No. 305/2003 and opposite party no. 1 in Civil Revision No. 974/2003.

15. In the result, the rule in Civil Revision No. 305/2003 is made absolute.

16. The rule issued in Civil Revision No. 974/2003 is discharged with costs. The order of stay passed earlier by this Court is hereby vacated.

Send down the lower court records at once.

End.

full_judgment:
N.K. Chakravartty, J: This rule at the instance of defendant-petitioners was issued calling upon the opposite party Nos. 1-5 to show cause as to why the impugned judgment and order dated 5.8.99 passed by the Senior Assistant Judge, Sadar Court, Khulna, in Title Suit No.109 of 1992 should not be set aside. Pending hearing of the rule all further proceedings of the aforesaid Title Suit was also stayed.

2. The short facts relevant for the purpose of disposal of this rule is that the plaintiffs -opposite parties on 9.5.92 instituted Title Suit No. 109 of 1992 in the Court of Senior Assistant Judge, Khulna praying for the following reliefs: (a) for declaration of their title to the land described in schedule 'Ka', (b) for declaration of the ex-parte judgment and decree dated 15.09.1972 passed in Title Suit No. 210 of 1969 are void, fraudulent and not binding upon the plaintiffs. Their case inter alia is that the defendant Nos. 1 to 3 obtained fraudulent decree in Title Suit No. 210 of 1969 on the plea that they along with the defendant No. 4 purchased the entire suit holding in auction vide certificate case No. 552- K.S/53-54 on 21.06.1954; the sale was set-aside by the decree passed in Title Suit No. 94 of 1961. Despite knowledge of the defendant Nos. 1 to 3 pleaded ignorance as to the decree passed in Title Suit No. 94 of 1961. The so called auction sale purchaser defendants were borgadars under the plaintiffs in the suit land which they acquired by way of successive transfer from the tenants and/or their heirs named in the C.S. Khatians. Summons of the Title Suit No. 210 of 1969 were suppressed and the plaintiffs (who were defendant Nos. 30 to 34 in Title suit No. 210 of 1969), were shown to have executed a petition of compromise in the Title Suit No. 210 of 1969 with fake signatures which the plaintiffs did not do.

3. That, the defendant Nos. 1 to 4, 16 and 17 appeared in the suit and submitted written statement denying all the plaint allegations and contending inter alia that 66.16 (30.92 khas and 35.25 tenanted) acres of land recorded in C.S. Khatian No. 232, which is the suit holding originally belonged to Umacharan and 8 others. Those tenants and/or their successors and assignee defaulted in paying rent for which the entire holding was sold in auction on 27.09.1954 vide certificate case No. 252/1953-54. The defendant Nos. 1 to 4 purchased the auction (defendant Nos. 1 to 3 to the extent of 8 annas jointly and defendant No.4 to the extent of rest 8 annas) and got delivery of possession through the process of law on 03.10.54. At the time of such auction purchase 43.53 acres of land was khas land of the holding; the defendant No.4 filed title suit No.117/1957 in the court sub-ordinate Judge, Khulna against the defendant No.1 to 3 for partition of her 1/2 (half) share out of Khas 43.53 acres of land of the holding and got decree on 12.09.1957 for the same. Since then she had been possessing her share separately while the defendant nos. 1 to 3 had been possessing their shares jointly. One Kamala Bala Dashi and others instituted Title Suit No. 94 of 1961 in the 1st Court of Munsiff, Khulna for setting aside the aforesaid auction sale on the plea of purchase from one of the decedents of original tenant and suppressing summons thereof obtained fraudulent decree dated 18.4.1964 beyond the knowledge of the auction purchasers. That, Samir Chardra Singha one of the full brothers of the plaintiffs purchased 1.00 acre of land by successive transfer from the defendant No.4, which was sold to the defendant No. 16 by Registered sale deed dated 25.8.1987; Satish Chandra Singha purchased 1.66 acres of land from the defendant No.4 by Registered sale deed dated 03.12.1957 and another 1.66 acres of land from the defendant Nos. 1 and 2 by Registered sale deed dated 08.03.1979 and by such purchase, father of the plaintiffs being in possession of 3.32 acres of land died leaving behind the plaintiffs and two other sons named Tapan and Samir. The plaintiffs and their brothers Tapan and Samir being is possession of the said 3.32 acres of land sold 1.66 acres of land jointly to Puspa Rani by Registered Sale Deed dated 04.07.1984 and delivered possession. Subsequently, the plaintiffs nos. 1, 2, 3, 5 and their full brothers Tapan and Samir jointly sold 1.66 acres of land to the defendant No. 17 and one Ranjit Kumar by Registered sale deed dated 30.07.1988. The claim of the plaintiffs as made out in the plaint has been waived and they have been estopped by executing and Registering sale deed dated 04.07.1984 and 30.7.1988 knowing of the fraudulent decree passed in title suit No. 94 of 1961, within time the defendant Nos. 1 to 3 instituted Title no. 210 of 1969 in the 1st Court of Munsiff, Khulna. The plaintiffs as defendant Nos. 30 to 34 of that suit on receipt of summons appeared in that suit but ultimately finding no defence, refrained from contesting the suit like other defendants. Ultimately Title Suit No 210 of 1969 was decreed ex-parte on 15.02.1972. One Sachindra Nath Das and others filed an application under Order 9 Rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 being Miscellaneous Case No.389 of 1972 for setting aside the decree dated 15.02.1972 passed in title suit no. 210 of 1969 which was ultimately dismissed on compromise. Again one Krishna Pada and others filed Miscellaneous Case No. 415 of 1974 under order 9 rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 for setting aside the decree dated 15.02.1972 passed in Title Suit No. 210 of 1969; which was also dismissed on compromise.

4. During continuation of the suits Sreemati Anna Roy, the defendant No. 3, died leaving behind 3 sons, the petitioner nos. 3 to 5 as her heirs, who were substituted in the suit by order No. 59 dated 19.07.1988.

5. In course of proceedings of the suit the defendant Nos. 1 to 4, 16 and 17 submitted an application praying for taking opinion of the Hand Writing Expert on comparing the siquantive and thumb impression of the plain-tiffs appearing on vokalatnama and petition of compromise submitted in Title Suit no. 210 of 1969, on Sale Deed No. 12243 dated 04.07.1984 and No. 167151 dated 30.07.1988. with the signature and thumb impression of the plaintiffs taken in court on physical appearance of the plaintiffs, contending inter alia that, the plaintiffs as defendant Nos. 30 and 34 appeared and compromised Title Suit no. 210 of 1969 upon which impugned decree dated 15.09.1972 was passed and that they transferred a portion of the suit land by sale deeds which has been denied by P.W. No. 1 during cross examination and that for proper determination of the suit taking such opinion is absolutely necessary.

6. The said application was heard on contest and was allowed by the trial court by judgment and order No. 81 dated 28.2.1999 directing the defendants for taking proper steps for the purpose.

7. On the next date i.e. on 23.03.1999 the said defendants submitted an application praying for directing the plaintiffs to appear in person in court for putting their signatures and thumb impression in presence of the Advocates of both the parties stating inter alia that all other steps in compliance with the courts' order dated 28.02.1999 were earlier taken.

8. After hearing both the parties the learned Assistant Judge, by his order No. 82 dated 23.03.1999 allowed the application and directed the plaintiffs to appear in person before the court for subscribing their signature and thumb impressions on 25.04.1999.

9. Instead of appearing on 17.05.1999 an application on behalf of the plaintiffs praying for exempting the plaintiff Nos. 1, 3 and 4 from personal appearance contending inter alia that plaintiff No.2 himself and as attorney of plaintiff No. 1 and the plaintiff No.5 himself and as attorney and plaintiff Nos. 3 and 4, instituted the suit for which they have Registered power of attorney.

10. Copy of the application (annexure-E) was received by the learned Advocate for the contesting defendants with the note of objection and there after on contested hearing the said prayer for exemption was rejected by order No.88 dated 13.06.1999 by the learned Senior Assistant Judge, with a direction on the plaintiffs to appear and subscribe simulative and thumb impression on 13.06.1999.

11. On 13.07.1999 another application was filed on behalf of the plaintiffs praying for exempting plaintiffs Nos. 1,3 and 4 from personal appearance and for sending signatures of those plaintiffs appearing on power of attorney given by them on the ground that those plaintiffs being resident in India would not be able to appear before the court physically.

12. The learned Advocate for the defendant-petitioners, under instruction of the defendants raised oral objection to the effect that signatures of the plaintiff Nos. 1,3 and 4 appearing on the so called power of attorney are neither genuine nor admitted by the defendants and as such it will be of no use, sending such signatures for Hand Writing Expert opinion. Unfortunately the objections were neither recorded nor discussed in the impugned judgment and order.

13. After hearing both the parties the learned Senior Assistant Judge, allowed the application by the impugned Judgment and order No. 88 dated 05.08.1999 assigning reasons.

14. Being aggrieved by the impugned judgment and order dated 05.08.1999 passed by the learned Assistant Judge, Sadar Court, Khulna, in Title Suit No. 109 of 1992, the defendant- petitioners preferred this revisional application under section 15 of the Code of Civil Procedure and obtained the Rule.

15. Mr. Qumrul Islam Siddique, learned Advocate, appears on behalf of the defendant-petitioners. Plaintiff opposite parties are being represented by Mr. M. Shamsul Alam along with Mr. A.K. Mainuddin and S.M. Aminul Islam, learned Advocates.

16. Mr. Siddique has taken three points before me. Firstly Mr. Siddique submits that, the learned Assistant Judge, committed error of law resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice in passing the impugned judgment and order having the effect of setting aside order No. 81 dated 28.2.1999, order No. 82 dated 23.3.1999 and order No. 86 dated 13.6.1999 without assigning any reason whatsoever.

17. Secondly, that the court below erred in law in passing the impugned judgment and order without recording objection of the defendant petitioners on the point, which resulted in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice.

18. Thirdly, that by the impugned judgment and order of taking opinion of Hand Writing Expert has been maintained and ordered on comparison between disputed signatures in absence of admitted signatures, which is inadmissible in evidence and which is an error of law occasioning failure of Justice in as much as Mr. Siddique by referring section 45 of the Evidence Act, 1872 further submits that the opinions of Experts on the question whether the two documents were writing by the same person or by different persons, are relevant.

19. Countering the aforesaid contentions Mr. M. Shamsul Alam submits that the plaintiffs institute the aforesaid suit after putting their respective signatures both upon plaint and upon Vokalotnama and that they also put their signatures upon the alleged solenama duly appearing in court. The defendant did not specifically denied those signatures of the plaintiffs in their written statement and as such this belated denial of signatures deserves no consideration now. Mr. Alam further submits that plaintiffs No. 1, 3 and 4 migrated to India duly authorising other plaintiffs to act on their behalf by executing Registered power of attorney and since they are not easily available and residing in foreign country they sought for exemption which was allowed by the court. According to Mr. Alam there are several admitted signatures of plaintiffs No. 1, 3 and 4 and it will be easy for any body as well as for the court to compare those signatures of the plaintiffs even by bringing volume books from the sub-registrar office. Mr. Alam lastly submits that after the close of the case of the plaintiffs this plea of the defendants is nothing but to delay the disposal of the suit.

20. Mr. A.K. Mainuddin appearing also on behalf of the plaintiff-opposite parties submits that mode of proving hand writing or signature: - It is not necessary that when ever a person denies signatures or hand writing in documents, it should be sent to an Expert for opinion. There are other modes of proving handwriting or signature as provided in sections 45 ,47, 67 and 73 of the Evidences Act. According to him the evidence of handwriting Expert is usually of a weak kind and it is unsafe.

21. Mr. Mainuddin further submits that when a document is produced by a party and the signature appearing there it is proved and subsequently the person concerned denies the signatures, it is the duty of the court to compare the same with his other admitted signatures on record.

22. Mr. Mainuddin referred to a decision of this court in the case of Gura Meah Shah and ors. Vs. Zahir Ahmed and ors. reported in 4 BLD (1984) at page 225. In that case it was held that order for personal appearance of a party--- whether the trial court can revise such order passed earlier-- A Court has always the discretion to revise such a direction and exempt a party from appearing personally and be satisfied with his appearance through Attorney— it can not be said that by the impugned order there has been a failure of justice affecting the merits of the case.

23. According to Mr. Mainuddin the defendant by filing written statements did not challenge the power of attorney and now at this belated stage the plea of the defendant is a mere plea only to harass the plaintiffs.

24. Now the only point for consideration is whether the trial court was justified in passing the impugned judgment and order?

25. I have very carefully gone through the pleadings of the parties, applications filed by the defendants for handwriting Expert opinion, and objection for exemption petition as well as perused the impugned judgment and order of the court below with the available materials on record. Wherefrom it reveals that the Court below while considering the prayer for Hand Writing Expert's opinion found that appearance of plaintiffs Nos. 1, 3 and 4 is necessary only to arrive at a final decision upon the controversy relating to solenama executed by them in Other Class Suit No. 210 of 1969 and accordingly allowed the prayer. But from the impugned order it transpires that subsequently on the prayer of the plaintiffs to the effect that they are not easily available and residing in foreign country and as such cannot be produced in Court as desired by the defendants. Plaintiffs have also clearly explained that there are several admitted signatures of the plaintiff nos. 1, 3 and 4 in plaint, Vokalat nama, power of attorney as well as Volume Books of Sub-Registry Office to compare the signatures with the disputed solenama. Moreover, other plaintiffs contesting the suit were also the signatories of the said solenama.

<u>26. In view of the facts and circumstances and submissions advanced by the opposite party it can be said that the opinion of an ex-pert is never binding on a Court. It is admitted in evidence only to help the Court in arriving at a correct decision. But it does not follow that the opinion of an expert is always correct. Genuineness of document how may be proved. The proof of the genuineness of a document is of the authorship of the document and is proof of a fact like that of any other fact. It may be proof of handwriting of the contents or of the signature. It may be proved by internal evidence afforded by the, contents of the documents. In an appropriate law the court may also be in a position to judge whether the document constitutes a genuine link in the chain of correspondence and thus to determine its authorship. The science of the study of calligraphy is inexact and has not yet attained any degree of accuracy. Hence the opinion of handwriting Expert should be received with great caution and it is unsafe to base a decision purely on expert opinion without sufficient corroboration.</u>

<u>27. The application praying for taking opinion of the handwriting Expert on comparing the siquantive and thumb impression of the plaintiffs appearing on Vokalatnama and petition of compromise submitted in Title Suit No. 210 of 1969, on Sale Deed No. 12243 dated 4.7.1984 and No. 167151 dated 30.7.1988 with the signature and thereby impression of the plaintiffs in Court on physical appearance of the plaintiffs is not necessary because of the fact that the plaintiffs as defendant Nos. 30 and 34 appeared and compromised Title Suit No. 210 of 1969 upon which impugned decree dated 15.9.1972 was passed and that they transferred a portion of the suit land by the registered sale deed so it can easily be compared in the naked eyes by any prudent man in assessing with the other evidences on record. Comparison of writing or signature with admitted writing or signature is a question of fact. Plaint or written statement after it has been filed in court and registered becomes a public document and thus the court is competent to form its opinion on a comparison of the handwritings and signatures appearing on the plaint, Vokalatnama, Registered power of attorney as well as registered sale deeds and Volume Books of S.R. office with the signatures appearing on the disputed solenama.</u>

28. In the instance case, it cannot be held that by making the impugned order there has been a failure of justice affecting the merits of the case. No interference is called for.

29. This disposes of all the contentions raised on behalf of the petitioners.

30. This rule is accordingly discharged without any order as to costs.

End.
